1. WT timecourse (TC) ATAC-seq

2. Cal-opa KD ATAC- and RNA-seq 

3. Cal-zld KD ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data 

4. Gene loci visualization

## Load Data used throughout the analysis

### Peaks
Peaks were called using open reads (<= 120 bp) from all WT NC11:LNC14 samples. These are the master peaks.
```{r, cache = FALSE}
load("../GRanges/peaks-32157.GRanges.R")
```

### all.coldata

Load the coldata data frame (df) containing meta data for all samples in each experiment set. 
```{r}
all.coldata <- as.data.frame(read_xlsx("../all-coldata.xlsx", sheet = 1, col_names = TRUE))

head(all.coldata)
```

## Annotation Data

This will be used throughout the analysis.

### All annotation data table

This table has all the information from the annotation; gene,features of a gene, seed ortholog, GOs,COgs,KEggs etc.
```{r}
merge.data.file <- "../Annotation_Data/Clogmia.MergedData.csv"
merge.data <- read.csv(merge.data.file)
#head(merge.data)
```

### blast data

This table contains the identified Drosophila melanogaster (Dme) homolgos from reciprocal blastp searches. Some notes: Not every transcript has a Dme hit. Sometimes there are ties, this can occur for similar amino acid sequences generated by transcript isoforms of the same gene or by paralogs. For ties the best 1:1 match will say "bidirectional" in the "Directionality" column and the name of that transcript will be listed in the "Cal HIT" column. Flybase IDs are included in the "flybase.id" column.
```{r}
blast.file <- "../Annotation_Data/Clogmia.blast.csv"
blast.data <- read.csv(blast.file)
row.names(blast.data)<-blast.data$ID
head(blast.data)
```

Combine the blast data and the merge data. This will be used later to find Dme homologs and other information for a gene of interest. The "Parent" column has the gene name. The gene can have features such a exons, transcripts,etc which are distinguished by the "ID" column. The "ID" column is unique. The DE analysis will use gene names corresponding to the "Parent" column. Generally the GO terms and COGs are assigned to the gene/parent not at the feature/transcript level. To find the Dme homolog "Dme HIT" for a gene you need to look at the transcript level. 
```{r}
all.annote.data <- merge(merge.data,blast.data, by.x = "ID", by.y ="ID", all.x = TRUE, all.y = TRUE)
# merge the two dfs by the ID column which is unique and matches 1:1
head(all.annote.data)
```



### Genome annotation gff3

Read in the gff3 file. This will be used for constructing the txdb for Clogmia albipunctata.
```{r}
gff3.file <- "../Annotation_Data/Clogmia_vNCBI.gff3"
```

### txdb of clogmia transcriptome 

Generate chromosome information to pass to the makeTxDbFromGFF function. There are six chromosomes that make up the assembly, they are 1,2,3,4,5,7. 
```{r}
calbi.chrom.info <- data.frame("chrom" = seqlevels(Calbipunctata),
                                  "length" = seqlengths(Calbipunctata),
                                  "is_circular" =
                                 isCircular(Calbipunctata),row.names = NULL)

```

Make calbi.txdb the txdb for Clogmia albipunctata (calbi.txdb) will be used to retrieve transcript(s),promoter, gene regions, etc for genes of interest.
```{r}

calbi.txdb <- GenomicFeatures::makeTxDbFromGFF(file = gff3.file,
                format = c("auto","gff3","gtf"), 
                dataSource = "2024 Annotation generated by the Schmidt-Ott lab at Univeristy of Chicago of the Calbipunctata_UNI4000 genome assembled in collaboration with Cantata Bio in 2023", 
                organism = "Clogmia albipunctata",
                taxonomyId = 85120,
                circ_seqs = NULL,
                chrominfo=calbi.chrom.info,
                miRBaseBuild=NA)
```

```{r}
genome(calbi.txdb) <- "ca6" # specify genome
```
##### *transcripts by gene*

For each gene extract all transcripts, then reduce to one transcript region per gene.  This will be used to generate RNA-seq counts per gene in later sections.
```{r}
transcripts.by.gene <- GenomicFeatures::transcriptsBy(calbi.txdb,by="gene")

transcripts.by.gene <- IRanges::reduce(transcripts.by.gene)

```





# Section 1 WT Timecourse ATAC-seq Analysis

### Background

Single embryo ATAC-seq data was performed spanning late syncytial development (NC11 - Late NC14) in the Clogmia albipunctata embryo. In this section we will measure changes in accessibility that occur throughout this developmental period and define dynamic peaks. We will categorize peaks based on where they are in the genome (genomic feature; exon, promoter, intron, intergenic). We will perform MEME analysis to identify putative factors acting at these regions.

Section overview

1. Classify peak by genomic feature 

Determine how many peaks correspond to putative intergenic or intronic enhancers, and promoters.

2. Determines how many peaks are open at each stage.

3. Perform differential enrichment analysis stage wise to identify major transitions in accessibility over time.

4. Cluster peaks into dynamic groups based on changes in accessibility. 

5. Perform Motif analysis


#### Data

#### WT Time course ATAC data

Open reads (<= 120 bp) for each sample individually
```{r, cache = FALSE}
load("../GRanges/wt-tc-openreads.GRanges.R")


genome(wt.tc.openreads) <- "ca6" # specify genome

```

Open reads (<= 120 bp) merged by stage
```{r ,cache = FALSE}
load("../GRanges/wt-tc-openreads-mereged-by-stage.GRanges.R")

```


#### Create WT TC ATAC-seq coldata

Sort all.coldata for the WT TC ATAC samples. The coldata will be used later in the DESeq2 analysis. 
```{r}
wt.coldata.atac <- all.coldata %>% filter(.,Experiment == "ATAC-TC") 

# factor each column

for (i in 1:ncol(wt.coldata.atac)){
    wt.coldata.atac[, i] = as.factor(wt.coldata.atac[, i])}

# set reference level for stage and treatment.group
wt.coldata.atac$treatment.group <- relevel(wt.coldata.atac$treatment.group,ref = "wt")

wt.coldata.atac$Stage <- factor(wt.coldata.atac$Stage, levels = c("NC11","NC12","NC13","NC14","LNC14"))

wt.coldata.atac$instrument.atac.data <- relevel(wt.coldata.atac$instrument.atac.data, ref = "NextSeq 500")

head(wt.coldata.atac)
```



## 1. Peaks by genome feature

What is the genomic distribution of the peaks? (Promoter, Intergenic, Intron, Exon)

This section will find peaks that overlap with a promoter, exon,intron or if a peak is intergenic. This information will be compiled into a table genomic.feature.peaks so genomic feature data can be pulled for a peak of interest.

Extract the following from the calbi.txdb.

Clogmia genes from the 
```{r}
calbi.genes <- GenomicFeatures::genes(calbi.txdb)
```

Promoters. Will use 500 bp upstream of TSS
```{r}
calbi.promoters <- GenomicFeatures::promoters(calbi.genes,upstream = 500, downstream = 10,use.names = TRUE)
calbi.promoters <- trim(calbi.promoters) # some regions are out of bounds, trim them
```

Introns 
```{r}

calbi.introns <- GenomicFeatures::intronsByTranscript(calbi.txdb)
calbi.introns <- unlist(calbi.introns) # unlist introns

```

Exons 
```{r}
calbi.exons <- GenomicFeatures::exonsBy(calbi.txdb,"tx")
calbi.exons <- unlist(calbi.exons) # unlist exons
```

##### Create a genomic.feature.peaks table

This table will contain the genomic feature information for a peak. Once made it will be added on to with promoter,exon,intron data.

First from the meta data of peaks get the peak name and original row number of each peak.

The row number is used later to restore peaks to their original row order.
```{r}
genomic.feature.peaks <- data.frame("peak.name" =  names(peaks.32157),
                     "original.row" = c(1:length(peaks.32157)))
head(genomic.feature.peaks)
```

##### Find overlaps with Promoters

Find peaks that overlap with a promoter. This will be done using the findOverlaps functions.

Create the peaks.promoters.overlaps.df.
```{r}
peaks.promoters.overlaps.df <- as.data.frame(findOverlaps(query = peaks.32157,subject = calbi.promoters))

head(peaks.promoters.overlaps.df)
```

Add peak.name column to the peaks.promoters.overlaps.df. Then add "Promoter" = TRUE column. Keep only unique peak.names, as some peaks overlap with more than one promoter region (likely bidirectional or because overlapping genes), we only need one entry per peak.
```{r}
peaks.promoters.overlaps.df <- peaks.promoters.overlaps.df %>% 
  mutate(.,peak.name = names(peaks.32157[queryHits])) %>%
   relocate(.,peak.name,.before = queryHits) %>%
  mutate(.,promoter=TRUE) %>% 
  relocate(.,promoter,.before = queryHits) %>% 
  distinct(., peak.name,promoter,queryHits)
  
head(peaks.promoters.overlaps.df)
```


Now add peaks.promoters.overlaps.df to genomic.feature.peaks df. Do this using the merge function, merging the dfs by peak.name. Keep all rows (all peaks) of the genomic.feature.peaks df. As a result a peak with a promoter hit will have  Promoter = TRUE and peaks with no hit will have Promoter = FALSE. 
```{r}
genomic.feature.peaks <- merge(x=genomic.feature.peaks,y=peaks.promoters.overlaps.df, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE)

#head(genomic.feature.peaks)
```

Sort the df by the original row.
```{r}
genomic.feature.peaks <- genomic.feature.peaks[order(genomic.feature.peaks$original.row), ]

head(genomic.feature.peaks)
```

Remove queryHits column.
```{r}
genomic.feature.peaks <- genomic.feature.peaks[,-(grep(colnames(genomic.feature.peaks),pattern = "queryHits"))]

```

Check that all peaks are in the table and in order. 
```{r}
all(names(peaks.32157) == genomic.feature.peaks$peak.name)
```


##### Find overlaps with Introns

The process will be repeated again for intronic regions.

Create the peaks.introns.overlaps.df.
```{r}
peaks.introns.overlaps.df <- as.data.frame(findOverlaps(query = peaks.32157,subject = calbi.introns))
```

Add peak.name column to the df, add intron = TRUE, remove duplicate peaks.
```{r}

peaks.introns.overlaps.df <- peaks.introns.overlaps.df %>% 
  mutate(.,peak.name = names(peaks.32157[queryHits])) %>%
   relocate(.,peak.name,.before = queryHits) %>%
  mutate(.,intron=TRUE) %>% 
  relocate(.,intron,.before = queryHits) %>% 
  distinct(., peak.name,intron,queryHits)

```

Add peaks.introns.overlaps.df to genomic.feature.peaks df.
```{r}
genomic.feature.peaks <- merge(x=genomic.feature.peaks,y=peaks.introns.overlaps.df, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE )

#Sort the new meta data by the original row

genomic.feature.peaks <- genomic.feature.peaks[order(genomic.feature.peaks$original.row), ]

#remove the queryhits column

genomic.feature.peaks <- genomic.feature.peaks[,-(grep(colnames(genomic.feature.peaks),pattern = "queryHits"))]

head(genomic.feature.peaks)
```

Check that the data is in the right order
```{r}
all(names(peaks.32157) == genomic.feature.peaks$peak.name)
```

##### Find overlaps with Exons.

Repeat the process for exons. 

Create the peaks.exons.overlaps.df.
```{r}
peaks.exons.overlaps.df <- as.data.frame(findOverlaps(query = peaks.32157,subject = calbi.exons))
```

Add peak.name column to the df, add exon = TRUE, remove duplicate peaks.
```{r}
 peaks.exons.overlaps.df <- peaks.exons.overlaps.df %>% 
  mutate(.,peak.name = names(peaks.32157[queryHits])) %>%
   relocate(.,peak.name,.before = queryHits) %>%
  mutate(.,exon=TRUE) %>% 
  relocate(.,exon,.before = queryHits) %>% 
  distinct(., peak.name,exon,queryHits)

```

Now add peaks.exons.overlaps.df. to genomic.feature.peaks.
```{r}
genomic.feature.peaks <- merge(x=genomic.feature.peaks,y=peaks.exons.overlaps.df, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE )

#Sort the new meta data by the original row

genomic.feature.peaks <- genomic.feature.peaks[order(genomic.feature.peaks$original.row), ]

#remove the queryhits
genomic.feature.peaks <- genomic.feature.peaks[,-(grep(colnames(genomic.feature.peaks),pattern = "queryHits"))]

head(genomic.feature.peaks)
```

Check that the data is in the right order.
```{r}
all(names(peaks.32157) == genomic.feature.peaks$peak.name)
```


And last...

Will add one final column "intergenic"

This will be a peak that does not overlap with a promoter, intron, nor exon.

Then we will clean up NAs in the columns of promoter,intron,exon, ie change to FALSE instead of NA. Then will add a genomic.feature columnthat consolidates the genomic feature of each peak.
```{r}
genomic.feature.peaks <- as.data.frame(genomic.feature.peaks) %>% 
  mutate(.,promoter =ifelse(is.na(promoter),"FALSE",promoter)) %>%
  mutate(.,intron =ifelse(is.na(intron),"FALSE",intron)) %>%  
  mutate(.,exon =ifelse(is.na(exon),"FALSE",exon)) %>%
  mutate(.,intergenic=if_else(promoter== FALSE & intron ==FALSE & exon ==FALSE,TRUE,FALSE)) %>% 
  relocate(.,intergenic, .after= peak.name) %>% 
  relocate(.,promoter, .after= intergenic) %>% 
  relocate(.,intron, .after= promoter) %>% 
  relocate(.,exon, .after= intron) %>% 
  mutate(genomic.feature = case_when(intergenic == TRUE ~ "intergenic",
                                   promoter == TRUE ~ "promoter",
                                   intron == TRUE & exon == FALSE & promoter == FALSE ~ "intron",
                                   exon == TRUE & intron == FALSE & promoter == FALSE ~ "exon",
                                   exon == TRUE & intron == TRUE & promoter == FALSE ~ "exon and intron")) %>% 
  relocate(.,genomic.feature, .after= exon) 


head(genomic.feature.peaks)

```


## 2. Peaks by stage 

Peaks were called for each stage (nuclear cycles) and a GRanges object has been constructed for each set.

For a final number of stage-specific peaks we will find peaks that are also recovered in the master peak list.

Then we will make a table. 
```{r ,cache = FALSE}

#Load the peaks for each stage GRanges 

load("../GRanges/nc11-peaks.GRanges.R")

load("../GRanges/nc12-peaks.GRanges.R")

load("../GRanges/nc13-peaks.GRanges.R")

load("../GRanges/nc14-peaks.GRanges.R")

load("../GRanges/lnc14-peaks.GRanges.R")
```

Use the countOverlaps function to determine if a peak is in the master peaks list, return a vector of TRUE or FALSE. This is done fore each nuclear cycle (NC).
```{r}
nc11.open.l <- as.logical(countOverlaps(query = peaks.32157, subject = nc11.peaks))

nc12.open.l <- as.logical(countOverlaps(query = peaks.32157, subject = nc12.peaks))

nc13.open.l <- as.logical(countOverlaps(query = peaks.32157, subject = nc13.peaks))

nc14.open.l <- as.logical(countOverlaps(query = peaks.32157, subject = nc14.peaks))

lnc14.open.l <- as.logical(countOverlaps(query = peaks.32157, subject = lnc14.peaks))
```


We will create a peaks open by stage table (peaks.open.by.stage). The df will have each peak listed and whether it is open at each stage.
```{r}
peaks.open.by.stage <- data.frame(peak.name = names(peaks.32157),
                                  open.at.NC11 = nc11.open.l,
                                  open.at.NC12 = nc12.open.l,
                                  open.at.NC13 = nc13.open.l,
                                  open.at.NC14 = nc14.open.l,
                                  open.at.LNC14 = lnc14.open.l)

head(peaks.open.by.stage)
```

We observe that the number of peaks generally increase as nuclear cycles progress. Except late in NC14 peaks when less peaks are called than at early NC14.
```{r}
paste0("NC11:",sum(peaks.open.by.stage$open.at.NC11 ==TRUE),
                               " NC12:",sum(peaks.open.by.stage$open.at.NC12 == TRUE),
                               " NC13:",sum(peaks.open.by.stage$open.at.NC13 == TRUE),
                               " NC14:",sum(peaks.open.by.stage$open.at.NC14 == TRUE),
                               " LNC14:",sum(peaks.open.by.stage$open.at.LNC14 == TRUE))
```

##### Peaks by stage and genomic feature 

We will table/plot the genomic distribution for all sets of peaks; all peaks, NC11, NC12, NC13, NC14, LNC14.

We observe that the genomic distribution of peaks shift slightly from stage to stage. 

See table/plots below.

## 3. DESeq2 analysis WT TC ATAC-seq data

We have done some simple characterization of the peaks. Now we want to understand how the accessibility of peaks changes from stage to stage. To determine this we will first perform differential enrichment analysis using DESeq2.

##### Counts ATAC Time course

A counts matrix of open reads (<=120 bp) in MACS identified master peaks will be made. 

This will be made by counting the overlaps of open reads (<= 120 bp) into a peak.

The counts matrix along with the sample data in coldata will be the input for DESeq2.
```{r}
wt.counts.atac <- lapply(wt.tc.openreads, function(x) countOverlaps(peaks.32157,x))

wt.counts.atac <- do.call("cbind",wt.counts.atac) # force the counts data into a table format where rows are peaks and columns are samples

head(wt.counts.atac)

```

The colnames of the counts table need to match the rownames of the wt.coldata.atac (created earlier in the document). Below assign the rownames of coldata to equal the colnames of counts.
```{r}
rownames(wt.coldata.atac) <- colnames(wt.counts.atac)

all(rownames(wt.coldata.atac) %in% colnames(wt.counts.atac))

all(rownames(wt.coldata.atac) == colnames(wt.counts.atac))
```

Filter counts. 

Before running DESeq2 we need to get rid of any peaks that have low or noisy counts.
```{r}
data.frame(sums = log2(rowSums(wt.counts.atac)+1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(sums)) +
  geom_density() +
 geom_vline(xintercept = 6.7) +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = 'Distribution of counts')
```

The number of peaks from the distribution above with counts less than 2^7.
```{r}
length(which(rowSums(wt.counts.atac) < 2^7))
```

The number of peaks with any count value of 0 or 1.
```{r}
table(apply(wt.counts.atac, 1, function(x) sum(x <= 1)))
```

We will filter peaks that have any count value of 0 or 1.
```{r}
wt.counts.atac <- wt.counts.atac[apply(wt.counts.atac, 1, function(x) !any(x <= 1)),]
```

The majority of the low count peaks from the distribution above are removed.
```{r}
length(which(rowSums(wt.counts.atac) < 2^7))
```

Check again that colnames of the counts table match the rownames of the wt.coldata.atac and are in the right order.
```{r}
all(rownames(wt.coldata.atac) %in% colnames(wt.counts.atac))

all(rownames(wt.coldata.atac) == colnames(wt.counts.atac))
```

##### Run WT ATAC DE Analysis

Now we have both inputs for DESeq2 analysis. The design component for the analysis will include the instrument the ATAC-seq data was sequenced on and the stage (NC). There are two batches of WT ATAC-seq data sequenced on different machines, this variable will be added to the DESeq2 analysis. We are interested in the changes in accessibility due to stage, this variable will be added last in the design.
```{r}
atac.dds1 <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = wt.counts.atac, colData = wt.coldata.atac, design = ~instrument.atac.data + Stage)
atac.dds1 <- DESeq(atac.dds1, parallel = FALSE)
```

Check that the names of results are as expected.
```{r}
resultsNames(atac.dds1)
```

Dispersion estimates. Take a look at dispersion to makes sure that the data fitting looks reasonable.
```{r}
plotDispEsts(atac.dds1)
```

##### Results

We will evaluate in stage wise comparisons how many peaks have a significant change in accessibility. And determine if the change in accessibility is up or down. 

Extract the results from DESeq2 using DESeq2::results make a df.
```{r}

nc12.v.nc11 <- as.data.frame(results(atac.dds1,contrast = c("Stage","NC12","NC11"),independentFiltering = FALSE))

nc13.v.nc12 <- as.data.frame(results(atac.dds1,contrast = c("Stage","NC13","NC12"),independentFiltering = FALSE))

nc14.v.nc13 <- as.data.frame(results(atac.dds1,contrast = c("Stage","NC14","NC13"),independentFiltering = FALSE))

lnc14.v.nc14 <- as.data.frame(results(atac.dds1,contrast = c("Stage","LNC14","NC14"),independentFiltering = FALSE))

```

##### MA plots

MA plot shows the log2 fold change (LFC) as a function of mean signal.
```{r}
nc12.v.nc11 %>% 
  mutate(sig = padj <= 0.05) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log10(baseMean), y = log2FoldChange, color = sig)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5,5)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" =  "black")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0,1,-1), linetype = 'dotted', color = 'blue') +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = "MA Plot nc12.v.nc11",
       x = "log10(mean counts)",
       y = "log2(FC)")

```

##### Volcano plots

To visually inspect the results of each comparison we make volcano plots.  For these plots significant changes in accessibility will be highlighted, and the number of peaks that go up or down will be quantified. The size of each data point will correspond to the intensity of the peak.

Statistical significance threshold is a LFC >= 1 or LFC <= -1 and an adjusted p-value (padj) <= 0.05.

```{r}
# 1. Update the logical 'sig' column to a 3-way 'Change' column (UP/DOWN/NS)
nc12.v.nc11 <- nc12.v.nc11 %>% 
  mutate(Change = case_when(
    is.na(padj) | padj > 0.05 | abs(log2FoldChange) < 1 ~ "NS",
    log2FoldChange <= -1 ~ "DOWN",
    log2FoldChange >= 1 ~ "UP"
  ))

# 2. Build the base plot using the matching theme and aesthetics
nc12.v.nc11.vol <- nc12.v.nc11 %>% 
  mutate(mean.intensity = baseMean / max(baseMean, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), color = Change, size = mean.intensity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) + # Adjusted to 0.3 to match previous
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-8, 8), ylim = c(0, 25)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN" = 'red', "UP" = "blue", "NS" = "grey")) +
  theme_clean(base_size = 12) + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(title = 'NC12 vs NC11 DA peaks')

# 3. Add the annotations using the safer sum() method
nc12.v.nc11.vol <- nc12.v.nc11.vol + 
  annotate("text", x = -1.5, y = 25, 
           label = sum(nc12.v.nc11$padj <= 0.05 & nc12.v.nc11$log2FoldChange <= -1, na.rm = TRUE)) + 
  annotate("text", x = 1.5, y = 25, 
           label = sum(nc12.v.nc11$padj <= 0.05 & nc12.v.nc11$log2FoldChange >= 1, na.rm = TRUE)) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 23, 
           label = sum(nc12.v.nc11$padj <= 0.05 & abs(nc12.v.nc11$log2FoldChange) < 1, na.rm = TRUE))

# Display the plot
nc12.v.nc11.vol

```

##### PCA 

We will make a PCA plot of PC 1 and PC2.
```{r}
rld <- rlog(atac.dds1, blind = FALSE) #rlog transform the data
pca <- plotPCA(rld, intgroup = c("Stage"), returnData = TRUE, ntop = 1000) # use the built in function plotPCA using only the top 1000 most variable regions
percentVar <- round(100 * attr(pca, "percentVar")) # calculate the variance attributed to each PC
```

We can see that PC1 correlates strongly with the stage of the embryos. For the most part replicates clusters nicely with other replicates of the same stage. Other notable sources of variance include the sex of the embryo. The chromosomes of Clogmia are isomorphic therefore embryo sex cannot be distinguished by the difference in the number of reads mapping to a sex chromosome. 
```{r}
PC12plot <- ggplot(pca, aes(PC1, PC2, color = Stage, shape = Stage)) + 
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 2) + 
  xlab(paste0("PC1: ", percentVar[1], "% variance")) + ylab(paste0("PC2: ", percentVar[2], "% variance")) + 
  stat_density_2d(h = 11, contour = TRUE, show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0.5, contour_var = "ndensity", bins = 4) +
  xlim(-35, 40) + 
  ylim(-30, 30) +
  #scale_color_manual(values = c("tomato", "blue")) + 
  theme(axis.line = element_line(color = "black")) + 
  theme_bw() +  
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = 'Principal Component Analysis')

PC12plot
```

## 4. Chromatin Acessibility Dynamics

The goal of this section is to determine 

1) How many dynamic peaks there are.

2) How the chromatin accessibility for each peak changes with each stage.

3) Identify patterns/clusters of peaks that share similar dynamics. 

##### Dynamic peaks 

Lets determine how many peak are dynamic using a statistical definition of a logFC >= 1 or logFC <= 1 and padj <= 0.05 in a least one DESeq2 comparison.

There are 6930 dynamic peaks (DAPs).
```{r}
sig.peak.names <- de.results.table[which(
  (de.results.table$padj.nc12.v.nc11 <= 0.05 &
  abs(de.results.table$lfc.nc12.v.nc11) >= 1) |
  (de.results.table$padj.nc13.v.nc12 <= 0.05 & abs(de.results.table$lfc.nc13.v.nc12) >= 1) |
  (de.results.table$padj.nc14.v.nc13 <= 0.05 & abs(de.results.table$lfc.nc14.v.nc13) >= 1) |
  (de.results.table$padj.lnc14.v.nc14 <= 0.05 & abs(de.results.table$lfc.lnc14.v.nc14) >= 1)
),"peak.name"]
```

Lets make a GRanges of the dynamic peaks. These are the peaks in the sig.peak.names vector.
```{r}
dynamic <- peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% sig.peak.names]


## check that the right peaks are labeled

#table(names(dynamic) %in% de.results.table$peak.name)

#all(names(dynamic) %in% sig.peak.names)

```

25227 peaks do not have significant changes in accessibility. 
```{r}
table(!names(peaks.32157) %in% names(dynamic))
```




Now lets evaluate how the accessibility of peaks change over time and if peaks cluster together based on chromatin accessibility dynamics.

To do this we will use the clustering algorithm degPatterns from DEGreport.


For the function we need to create a normalized count matrix from the DESeq2 object.  We will cluster all dynamic peaks identified previously ie the peaks that have some significant change in accessibility.
```{r}
res.atac <- results(atac.dds1)

sig.res.atac <- res.atac[rownames(res.atac) %in% names(dynamic),]

#table(names(dynamic) %in% rownames(res.atac))

#table(rownames(res.atac) %in% names(dynamic))
```


Now the count matrix needs to be transformed using the rlog transformation.
```{r}
rm(rld) # if necessary, remove the rld object created for the pca plot, 

rld <- rlog(atac.dds1, blind = TRUE) # transform the data with blind = TRUE
```

Extract the normalized matrix.
```{r}
rld.mat.atac <- assay(rld)
```

Keep only the significant peaks.
```{r}
sig.rld.mat.atac <- rld.mat.atac[rownames(sig.res.atac),]

#table(names(dynamic) == rownames(sig.rld.mat.atac))

#table(rownames(sig.rld.mat.atac) == names(dynamic))

```

Now that we have the matrix we can run degPatterns. Peaks will be clustered using a z-score. [For more see the manual](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/DEGreport.html).

To cluster peaks we will specify the minimum number of peaks in a group (minc) as 10. We will skip this part to save time, the saved results can be found in "./WT_timecourse/patterns-group-table.txt"

```{r eval=FALSE}
patterns <- degPatterns(sig.rld.mat.atac, metadata = colData(atac.dds1), time = "Stage", minc = 10, col = NULL)
```

##### Dynamic group plot 

We observe that there is a lot of fluctuation/ volatility in the accessibility of peak that was not appreciated in the stage-wise comparisons. In other words, there are more complex dynamics than progressive losses or gains in accessibility from stage to stage. These dynamics could reflect the activity of the cis-regulatory element. 
```{r, fig.height=7,fig.width=7, eval=FALSE}
patterns$plot
```

Save plot fo file
```{r eval=FALSE}
pdf(file = "../Plots/dynamic-groups.pdf", width = 10,height = 7)

patterns$plot

dev.off()
```

## 5. MOTIF Analysis

Motif enrichment analysis using MEME will be performed to identify potential factors acting on these regions. 

In addition motifs for factors of interest, Zld and Opa will be searched for in the peaks using seqLogo::matchPWM.

#### MEME

##### MEME all peaks

Get sequences for peaks using the function below. 

For each peak, the peak will be centered on the summit and the length will be normalized to 100 bp. The sequence of this region is extracted from the Calbipunctata object using the getSeq function.
```{r}
genome(Calbipunctata) <- "ca6" # set genome of Calbipunctata

get.my.seqs <- function(p, name, dir){
    #regions = p[mcols(p)[subset][, 1]]
    #regions  = p[p %in% subset]
    regions = p
    start(regions) = regions$max
    end(regions) = regions$max
    regions = resize(regions, width = 100, fix = "center")
    regionseqs = getSeq(Calbipunctata, regions)
    export(regionseqs, con = paste0(dir, "/", name, ".txt"), format = "fasta")
}
```


*Sequence of all peaks*
```{r}
# dir for output
sequence.output.directory <-"../MEME"

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157, dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "peaks-32157")

```



*Sequence of all NC11:LNC14 peaks*

```{r}
get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[nc11.open.l], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "nc11-peaks-q1e25")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[nc12.open.l], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "nc12-peaks-q1e25")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[nc13.open.l], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "nc13-peaks-q1e25")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[nc14.open.l], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "nc14-peaks-q1e25")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[lnc14.open.l], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "lnc14-peaks-q1e25")
```


Get background sequences

MEME also needs a set of background sequences to run. For all peak we will use a random set of genomic regions where there are no peaks. 

Tile the Clogmia genome.
```{r}
ca.10bp <- tileGenome(seqlengths(BSgenome.Calbipunctata.Cantata.uni4000), tilewidth = 10, cut.last.tile.in.chrom = TRUE)
```

We will only consider the 6 chromosome sized scaffolds. Update the seqinfo for the tiled genome objected (ca.10bp)
```{r}
good.uns <- seqlevels(peaks.32157) 
#good.uns
```

```{r}
ca.10bp <- ca.10bp[seqnames(ca.10bp) %in% good.uns]
seqlevels(ca.10bp) <- seqlevels(peaks.32157)
seqinfo(ca.10bp) <- seqinfo(peaks.32157)
seqlevels(ca.10bp) <- seqlevelsInUse(ca.10bp)

```

First we get a set of regions (bins) where there are no neighboring peaks. Then the regions are resized to 100 bp and 1000 regions are sampled. The regions are named corresponding to the genomic coordinate. The sequences are then exported using the getSeq and export functions.
```{r}
emptyBins <- ca.10bp[!as.logical(countOverlaps(ca.10bp, resize(peaks.32157, width = 10000, fix = "center")))]

set.seed(124) # set seed for sampling 

selectBins <- resize(sample(emptyBins, size = 1000, replace = FALSE), width = 100, fix = "center")

names(selectBins) <- paste0(seqnames(selectBins),":",start(selectBins),"-",end(selectBins))

controlSeqs <- getSeq(Calbipunctata,selectBins)


export(controlSeqs, con = "../MEME/WT_Tc_control-seq.txt", format = "fasta")

```

#### Find PWM 

In subsequent sections we will explore the effects of Cal-zld and Cal-opa depletion on chromatin accessibility in the Clogmia embryo. Below we will identify peaks with a Zld and or Opa motif.


In the following sections the raw count matrix from a binding assay will be loaded (column order is  "A","C","G","T", row order is DNA positions 1-n). The raw matrix will be converted to a frequency matrix. From the frequency matrix a seqlogo of the PWM in both orientations will be made and trimmed to the positions that contain the most information. The trimmed PWM will be used in the findPWM function to identify peaks with a 80% match to the PWM. For a Dme-Zld data comes from a solex binding assay. The Opa matrix is from Dme ATAC-seq study which found a Dme-Opa motif enriched in late NC14 ATAC-seq peaks (Soluri et al. elife 2020) 

##### Zld 
```{r}
zldPWM <- read.delim("../PWMs/vfl_SOLEXA_5_FBgn0259789_raw.txt",header = FALSE)

head(zldPWM)
```

```{r}
zldPWM <- signif((zldPWM/rowSums(zldPWM)), digits = 8) # convert to frequencies

# included an obnoxious amount of sig digits so that every value sums to one
apply(zldPWM,1,sum)
```

```{r}
zldPWM <- as.matrix(zldPWM)
colnames(zldPWM) <- c("A","C","G","T") # add col names

tzldPWM<- t(zldPWM) # transpose
seqLogo(tzldPWM)
```

```{r}
zldPWM <- zldPWM[5:12,] # will trim off the low information positions
tzldPWM <- t(zldPWM)

seqLogo(tzldPWM)
```

Save PWM.
```{r}
pdf(file = "../Plots/zld-dme.pdf", width = 6,height = 5)

seqLogo(tzldPWM)

dev.off()
```

```{r}
tzldPWMRevCom <- t(reverseComplement(zldPWM))
seqLogo(tzldPWMRevCom)
```

Now we will get sequences for peaks, this sequence will be searched for the PWM using matchPWM.
```{r}
genome(Calbipunctata) <- "ca6"
seq.peaks <- getSeq(Calbipunctata,peaks.32157)

```

Zld PWM in peaks. We will search both strands.
```{r}
zld.peak <- lapply(seq.peaks, function(x){
  matchPWM(tzldPWM, subject = x, min.score = "80%",with.score = TRUE)
})

zld.peak.rc <- lapply(seq.peaks, function(x){
  matchPWM(tzldPWMRevCom, subject = x, min.score = "80%",with.score = TRUE)
})
```

Create a vector of peaks with a match.
```{r}
# peaks with at least one match will have a length greater than 0
n.zld.peak <- zld.peak[lengths(zld.peak) > 0] 
n.zld.peak.rc <- zld.peak.rc[lengths(zld.peak.rc) > 0]
```

Peaks with at least one Zld motif.
```{r eval=FALSE}
length(unique(c(names(n.zld.peak),names(n.zld.peak.rc))))
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
paste0("percent of peaks with a zld motif ",
       round(length(unique(c(names(n.zld.peak),names(n.zld.peak.rc))))/(length(peaks.32157))*100,1),"%")


```

This is already a frequency matrix.

```{r}
opaPWM <- as.matrix(read.table("../PWMs/Opa_PWM_from_ATAC_wt_late_MEME.txt", header = FALSE, sep =" "))

colnames(opaPWM) <- c("A","C","G","T")

#is.matrix(opaPWM)

seqLogo(topaPWM)
```

```{r}
topaPWM <- t(opaPWM)
#topaPWM
seqLogo(topaPWM)
```

```{r }
seqLogo(topaPWMRevCom)
```

Opa PWM in peaks. We will search both strands.
```{r}

  matchPWM(topaPWM, subject = x, min.score = "80%",with.score = TRUE)
})

opa.peak.rc <- lapply(seq.peaks, function(x){
  matchPWM(topaPWMRevCom, subject = x, min.score = "80%",with.score = TRUE)
})
```


Create a vector of peaks with a match.
```{r}
# peaks with at least one match will have a length greater than 0
n.opa.peak <- opa.peak[lengths(opa.peak) > 0] 
n.opa.peak.rc <- opa.peak.rc[lengths(opa.peak.rc) > 0] 
```

Peaks with at least one Opa motif.


```{r}
paste0("percent of peaks with an opa motif ",
       round(length(unique(c(names(n.opa.peak),names(n.opa.peak.rc))))/(length(peaks.32157))*100,1),"%")
```

##### Motif table

Create a motif table denoting if a peak has a Zld or Opa motif.

Create a logical vector of peaks with a match on the forward or reverse strand for both motifs.
```{r}
opa.peaks.l <- names(peaks.32157) %in% names(n.opa.peak)
opa.peaks.rc.l <- names(peaks.32157) %in% names(n.opa.peak.rc)

zld.peaks.l <- names(peaks.32157) %in% names(n.zld.peak)
zld.peaks.rc.l <- names(peaks.32157) %in% names(n.zld.peak.rc)

```

Construct the df.
```{r}
motif.table <- data.frame(peak.name = names(peaks.32157),
                          opa.sites = opa.peaks.l, 
                          opa.sites.rc = opa.peaks.rc.l, 
                          zld.sites = zld.peaks.l, 
                          zld.sites.rc = zld.peaks.rc.l)


head(motif.table)
```



### Save results section 1

Tables

The data that summarizes this section are in 5 dfs

1. peaks.open.by.stage with the number of peaks called in each stage

2. The de.results.table containing the WT timecourse DESeq2 results 

3. The patterns.group.table of dynamic peaks and the dynamic peak groups

# Section 2 Cal-Opa

### Background

ATAC-seq was performed on Cal-opa RNAi (specific to the maternal transcript) embryos at NC12 and NC13. RNA was isolated from the ATAC preps and made into RNA-seq libraries. Several control groups were collected for these experiments. 1) Wild-type (WT): untreated  embryos. 2) Alignment controls: aligned on the injected slide and not injected. 3) injection controls: aligned on the injected slide and injected with dsRNA targeting dsred. Successful Cal-opa knockdown is determined from the RNA-seq data by a fold change (FC) calculation. The FC calculation of Cal-opa mRNA levels is conducted with the average of control embryos (untreated wild-type and alignment controls) from the same experimental date (embryo batch) as reference. Cal-opa RNAi embryos with a FC < 0.25 (knockdown efficiency greater than 75%) were used for further analysis.

Differential enrichment analysis on the ATAC- and RNA-seq data at both timepoints will be performed using DESeq2. The DESeq2 model will be generated from all experimental groups so that wide range of variance stemming from "genotype" and technical manipulation is accounted for. In the text only the results of the Cal-opa KDs vs alignment control (ac) comparison is reported for both ATAC and RNA-seq DE analysis. This serves to simplify reporting and avoids masking the real biological effects. 



Section overview:

1. Identify Cal-opa KDs at NC12 and NC13

2. DESeq2 analysis setup.

3. NC12 DE analysis of RNA-seq data and ATAC-seq data. 

Identify significant differentially  expressed genes (DE genes/degs) upon Cal-opa KD. Identify significant differentially accessible (DA peaks/ daps) upon Cal-opa KD.

4. NC13 DE analysis of RNA-seq data and ATAC-seq data. 

Identify significant differentially expressed genes (DE genes/degs) upon Cal-opa. Identify significant differentially accessible (DA peaks/ daps) upon Cal-opa KD.

5. Motif enrichment analysis of DA peaks using MEME.

6. Identify Cal-Opa targets at NC12 and NC13. 

Identify how many degs are transcription factors (TFs). In the annotation data the GO term "GO:0003700" for TF and COG symbol "K" for transcription is used to identify these genes. Identify "key" Cal-Opa targets. Key Cal-Opa targets will be identified as DE TFs whose loci has one or more Opa motif positive Cal-Opa sensitive ATAC-seq peaks.

7. Evaluate how Bicoid (Bcd) targets are affected by Cal-Opa depletion in Clogmia

Addendum 8. Repeat of NC12 analysis with one injection control outlier removed.


Hence forth Cal-opa/Cal-Opa may be shortened to opa/Opa.

## 1. Identify knockdowns

Now we will identify KDs by calculating the fold change (FC) of opa for each sample for both stages.

First we create a count matrix of RNA-seq counts per gene. 

Then we create a CPM matrix that will be used in the fold change calculation.

The FC calculation of Cal-opa mRNA levels is conducted with the average of control embryos (untreated wild-type and alignment controls) from the same embryo batch (experimental date) as reference.


In the annotation of Clogmia albipunctata the opa gene is "evm.TU.scaffold_7.878".

##### RNA counts matrix


We will first generate a RNA counts matrix of sample counts per gene.  

We will use the countOverlap function to count RNA-seq reads within the gene transcript (transcripts.by.gene). 

The count matrix will be normalize CPM for the FC calculation

The raw counts matrix will be used for DESeq2 analysis (in proceeding sections). 



NC12
```{r}
nc12.opakd.counts.rna <- lapply(opakd.nc12.rnaseq, function(x) countOverlaps(transcripts.by.gene,x))
nc12.opakd.counts.rna <- do.call("cbind",nc12.opakd.counts.rna) # force the counts data into a table format where rows are genes and columns are samples

head(nc12.opakd.counts.rna[,1:6])
```

NC13
```{r}
nc13.opakd.counts.rna <- lapply(opakd.nc13.rnaseq, function(x) countOverlaps(transcripts.by.gene,x))
nc13.opakd.counts.rna <- do.call("cbind",nc13.opakd.counts.rna) # force the counts data into a table format where rows are genes and columns are samples

head(nc13.opakd.counts.rna[,1:6])
```

Now we will CPM normalize the count data for each stage.

NC12
```{r}
nc12.opakd.colsums <- colSums(nc12.opakd.counts.rna) # total counts for each sample


nc12.opakd.cpm <- sweep(x = nc12.opakd.counts.rna, MARGIN = 2, STATS = nc12.opakd.colsums, FUN = '/') # For each sample divide each count by the total counts

nc12.opakd.cpm <- nc12.opakd.cpm*1e6 # Multiple by 1M to get CPM


table(round(colSums(nc12.opakd.cpm))) # double check the sum is 1M
```

NC13
```{r}
nc13.opakd.colsums <- colSums(nc13.opakd.counts.rna) # total counts for each sample

nc13.opakd.cpm <- sweep(x = nc13.opakd.counts.rna, MARGIN = 2, STATS = nc13.opakd.colsums, FUN = '/')  # For each sample divide each count by the total counts

nc13.opakd.cpm <- nc13.opakd.cpm*1e6 # Multiple by 1M to get CPM

table(round(colSums(nc13.opakd.cpm))) # double check the sum is 1M
```


We will create a FC df (fc.table) for each stage containing the sample name, treatment group, embryo batch (Experiment.Date) and opa CPMs.

Starting with NC12.

#### FC calculation NC12
```{r}
nc12.fc.table <- data.frame(Sample.name.full = nc12.opakd.coldata.rna$Sample.name.full,
                            treatment.group = nc12.opakd.coldata.rna$treatment.group,
                            Experiment.Date = nc12.opakd.coldata.rna$Experiment.Date,
                            opa.cpm=nc12.opakd.cpm["evm.TU.scaffold_7.878",])
```

Get the averaged opa CPM for control samples (wt and alignment) by embryo batch.
```{r}

opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date.nc12 <- nc12.fc.table %>% 
  filter(.,treatment.group == "wt" | treatment.group == "alignment control") %>% 
  group_by(.,Experiment.Date) %>% 
  summarize(.,mean(opa.cpm))


```

Add the averaged control CPM to the fc.table, each will have a column. Then perform the FC calculation by dividing each sample's CPM by the control CPM from the the same embryo batch. Add the result to the fc.table, producing the the column called "FC".
```{r}
nc12.fc.table <- nc12.fc.table %>% 
mutate(., opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.230518 = rep(opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date.nc12[[1,2]],nrow(nc12.fc.table)),
opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.230627 = rep(opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date.nc12[[2,2]],nrow(nc12.fc.table)),
opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.230629 = rep(opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date.nc12[[3,2]],nrow(nc12.fc.table))) %>% 
  mutate(., FC =case_when(
  Experiment.Date == "230518" ~ opa.cpm/opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.230518,
  Experiment.Date == "230627" ~ opa.cpm/opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.230627,
  Experiment.Date == "230629" ~ opa.cpm/opa.cpm.wt.ac.avg.230629))

```


Plot

```{r}
color.code <-c("wt" = "#50ad9f","alignment control" = "#0000A2","injection control"="#bc272d", "opa"="#e9c716") 

 nc12.fc.table %>% ggplot(., aes(x= treatment.group, y = FC, fill = treatment.group)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 3,shape = 21, color = "black",width=0.2)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = color.code) +
  ylim(-0.2,2) +  
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.25, linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1),
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```


4 Cal-opa RNAi embryos have a FC < 0.25

## 2. DE Analysis Setup

#### Update coldatas and counts.rna

Now that KDs have been identified the coldata should be updated.

Add a genotype column to coldata. For the opa treatment group an embryo's  genotype will be either opa, intKD or noKD based on the FC; FC < 0.25 is a KD (opa), 0.25 < FC < 0.5 intermediate KD (intKD) and FC > 0.5 is no KD (noKD). For the control treatment groups, genotype is equal to the treatment group, but written in short hand.

*NC12*

Add the colnames of the RNA counts to the rownames of coldata.rna
```{r}
rownames(nc12.opakd.coldata.rna) <- colnames(nc12.opakd.counts.rna)
```

Add the FC to the coldatas and add a genotype column. 

Starting with coldata.rna
```{r}

nc12.opakd.coldata.rna <- cbind(nc12.opakd.coldata.rna, FC = nc12.fc.table$FC)

nc12.opakd.coldata.rna <- nc12.opakd.coldata.rna %>%
  mutate(genotype = case_when(
  treatment.group == "wt"  ~ "wt",
  treatment.group == "alignment control" ~ "ac",
  treatment.group == "injection control" ~ "dsred",
  (treatment.group == "opa" & FC > 0.5) ~ "noKD",
  (treatment.group == "opa" & 0.25 < FC & FC < 0.5) ~ "intKD",
   (treatment.group == "opa" & FC < 0.25) ~ "opa")) %>% 
  relocate(.,genotype,.after = treatment.group)

# factor columns
for (i in 1:ncol(nc12.opakd.coldata.rna)){
    nc12.opakd.coldata.rna[, i] = as.factor(nc12.opakd.coldata.rna[, i])
}

# Set the reference levels
nc12.opakd.coldata.rna$treatment.group <- relevel(nc12.opakd.coldata.rna$treatment.group,ref = "alignment control")

nc12.opakd.coldata.rna$genotype <- relevel(nc12.opakd.coldata.rna$genotype,ref = "ac")

nc12.opakd.coldata.rna$Experiment.Date <- relevel(nc12.opakd.coldata.rna$Experiment.Date,ref = "230627")

head(nc12.opakd.coldata.rna)

```

```{r}
return(open100.binavg)
```

#### Filter RNA counts

Before proceeding with the DESeq2 analysis, the RNA-seq counts need to be filtered to remove noisy and no count genes. This will be done by plotting the distribution of counts, which will show the true distribution and the noise. A cutoff based on the count distribution will be applied to remove any counts below those values.

NC12 
```{r}
data.frame(means = log2(rowMeans(nc12.opakd.counts.rna)+1)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(means)) +
  geom_density() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4) +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = 'Distribution of rna counts NC12 opaKD experiment')
```

Remove any gene counts below 2^4.
```{r}
nc12.opakd.counts.rna <- nc12.opakd.counts.rna[rowMeans(nc12.opakd.counts.rna) > 2^4,]
```

Again check that the colnames in the counts matrix match the rownames in coldata.
```{r}
all(colnames(nc12.opakd.counts.rna) == rownames(nc12.opakd.coldata.rna))
```

NC13
```{r}
data.frame(means = log2(rowMeans(nc13.opakd.counts.rna)+1)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(means)) +
  geom_density() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 4) +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = 'Distribution of rna counts NC13 opa KD experiment')
```

Remove any gene counts below 2^4.
```{r}
nc13.opakd.counts.rna <- nc13.opakd.counts.rna[rowMeans(nc13.opakd.counts.rna) > 2^4,]
```

Again check that the colnames in the counts matrix match the rownames in coldata.
```{r}
all(colnames(nc13.opakd.counts.rna) == rownames(nc13.opakd.coldata.rna))
```

#### Filter ATAC counts

Before running DESeq2 we need to get rid of any peaks that have low or noisy counts.

NC12 
```{r}
data.frame(sums = log2(rowSums(nc12.opakd.counts.atac)+1)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(sums)) +
  geom_density() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5.5) +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = 'Distribution of atac counts NC12 opaKD experiment')
```

The number of peaks from the distribution above with counts less than 2^5.5.
```{r}
length(which(rowSums(nc12.opakd.counts.atac) < 2^5.5))
```

The number of peaks with any count value of 0 or 1.
```{r}
table(apply(nc12.opakd.counts.atac, 1, function(x) sum(x <= 1)))
```

We will filter peaks that have any count value of 0 or 1.
```{r}
nc12.opakd.counts.atac <- nc12.opakd.counts.atac[apply(nc12.opakd.counts.atac, 1, function(x) !any(x <= 1)),]
```

This removes low count peaks form the distribution above.
```{r}
length(which(rowSums(nc12.opakd.counts.atac) < 2^5.5))
```

Again check that the colnames in the counts matrix match the rownames in coldata.
```{r}
all(colnames(nc12.opakd.counts.atac) == rownames(nc12.opakd.coldata.atac))
```


Repeat for NC13

## 3. NC12 DE Analysis 

The design component for RNA-seq and ATAC-seq the DESeq2 analysis with be the same. The design component will include embryo batch (Experiment.Date) and genotype. We are interested in the changes in expression/accessibility due to genotype, this variable will be added last in the design.

#### NC12 DESeq2 RNA-seq data
```{r}
nc12.rna.dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = nc12.opakd.counts.rna, colData = nc12.opakd.coldata.rna, design = ~ Experiment.Date + genotype)

nc12.rna.dds <- DESeq(nc12.rna.dds, parallel = FALSE)

```

Check that the names of results are as expected.
```{r}
resultsNames(nc12.rna.dds)
```

Dispersion estimates. Take a look at dispersion to makes sure that the data fitting looks reasonable.
```{r}
plotDispEsts(nc12.rna.dds)
```

Results 

##### NC12 opa KD vs alignment control DE genes
```{r}
nc12.res.opa.ac.rna <- as.data.frame(results(nc12.rna.dds, contrast = c("genotype", "opa", "ac"), independentFiltering = FALSE))
```

Add a column indicating if a gene is significantly differentially expressed.

Significant DEGs will be genes with a LFC >= 1 or LFC <=-1 and a padj <= 0.05
```{r}
nc12.res.opa.ac.rna <- nc12.res.opa.ac.rna %>% 
  mutate(.,Sig = if_else((padj <= 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >=1),TRUE,FALSE))
```

Add a column, "Change", indicating if the change in expression was up or down.
```{r}
nc12.res.opa.ac.rna <- nc12.res.opa.ac.rna %>% mutate(Change = case_when(
  is.na(log2FoldChange) == TRUE | Sig == FALSE ~ "NA",
  log2FoldChange < 0 ~ "DOWN",
  log2FoldChange > 0 ~ "UP"))
```

Add a column, "gene.locus", with the gene name.
```{r}
nc12.res.opa.ac.rna <- nc12.res.opa.ac.rna %>% mutate(gene.locus = rownames(.))
```

MA Plot
```{r}
nc12.res.opa.ac.rna %>% 
  mutate(sig = padj <= 0.05) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log10(baseMean), y = log2FoldChange, color = sig)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5,5)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" =  "black")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0,1,-1), linetype = 'dotted', color = 'blue') +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = "MA Plot nc12.res.opa.ac.rna",
       x = "log10(mean counts)",
       y = "log2(FC)")

```

Lets plot the result and highlight significant DEGs. For this plot sig DEGs will be highlighted, and the number of DEGs that go up or down will be quantified.
```{r }
# pdf("../Plots/nc12_opa_ac_rna_volcano_plot_clean.pdf", width = 4, height = 3)


nc12.opa.ac.rna.vol.rna <- nc12.res.opa.ac.rna %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), color = Change, size = mean.intensity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 3) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-10, 10), ylim = c(0, 70)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log2(c(0.5, 2)), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN" = 'red', "UP" = "blue", "NS" = "grey")) +
  theme_clean(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "none")+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  
  labs(title = 'opaKD vs AC')

nc12.opa.ac.rna.vol.rna  +  
  annotate(geom = "text", x = -5, y = 50, label = length(which(nc12.res.opa.ac.rna$padj <= 0.05 & nc12.res.opa.ac.rna$log2FoldChange <= -1))) +  
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 5, y = 50, label = length(which(nc12.res.opa.ac.rna$padj <= 0.05 & nc12.res.opa.ac.rna$log2FoldChange >= 1))) +
  annotate(geom = 'text', x = 0, y = 49, label = length(which(nc12.res.opa.ac.rna$padj <= 0.05 & abs(nc12.res.opa.ac.rna$log2FoldChange) < 1)))
#dev.off()
```

## 4. NC13 DE Analysis 

The design component for RNA-seq and ATAC-seq the DESeq2 analysis with be the same. The design component will include embryo batch (Experiment.Date) and genotype. We are interested in the changes in expression/accessibility due to genotype, this variable will be added last in the design.


#### NC13 DESeq2 RNA-seq data
```{r}
nc13.rna.dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = nc13.opakd.counts.rna, colData = nc13.opakd.coldata.rna, design = ~ Experiment.Date + genotype)
nc13.rna.dds <- DESeq(nc13.rna.dds, parallel = FALSE)
```


Check that the names of results are as expected.
```{r}
resultsNames(nc13.rna.dds)
```

Dispersion estimates. Take a look at dispersion to makes sure that the data fitting looks reasonable.
```{r}
plotDispEsts(nc13.rna.dds)
```

Results 

##### NC13 opaKD vs alignemnt control DE genes
```{r}
nc13.res.opa.ac.rna <- as.data.frame(results(nc13.rna.dds, contrast = c("genotype", "opa", "ac"), independentFiltering = FALSE))
```

Add a column indicating, “Sig”, if a gene is significantly differentially expressed.

Significant DEGs will be genes with a LFC >= 1 or LFC <=-1 and a padj <= 0.05
```{r}
nc13.res.opa.ac.rna <- nc13.res.opa.ac.rna %>% mutate(.,Sig = if_else((padj <= 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >=1),TRUE,FALSE))
```

Add a column “Change”, indicating if the change in expression was up or down.
```{r}
nc13.res.opa.ac.rna <- nc13.res.opa.ac.rna %>% mutate(Change = case_when(
  is.na(log2FoldChange) == TRUE | Sig == FALSE ~ "NA",
  log2FoldChange < 0 ~ "DOWN",
  log2FoldChange > 0 ~ "UP"))
```

Add a column, "gene.locus", with the gene name.
```{r}
nc13.res.opa.ac.rna <- nc13.res.opa.ac.rna %>% mutate(., gene.locus = rownames(.))
```


MA plot
```{r}
nc13.res.opa.ac.rna %>% 
  mutate(sig = padj <= 0.05) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log10(baseMean), y = log2FoldChange, color = sig)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5,5)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" =  "black")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0,1,-1), linetype = 'dotted', color = 'blue') +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = "MA Plot nc13.res.opa.ac.rna",
       x = "log10(mean counts)",
       y = "log2(FC)")
```



Lets plot the result and highlight significant DEGs. For this plot sig DEGs will be highlighted, and the number of DEGs that go up or down will be quantified.
```{r }
#pdf("../Plots/nc13_opa_ac_rna_volcano_plot_clean.pdf", width = 4, height = 3)

nc13.opa.ac.vol.rna <- nc13.res.opa.ac.rna %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), color = Change, size = mean.intensity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size=3) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-10, 10), ylim = c(0, 70)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log2(c(0.5, 2)), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN" = 'red', "UP" = "blue", "NA" = "grey")) +
  theme_clean(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "none")+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()
  ) +labs(title = 'opaKD vs AC')

nc13.opa.ac.vol.rna  + 
  annotate(geom = "text", x = -5, y = 50, label = length(which(nc13.res.opa.ac.rna$padj <= 0.05 & nc13.res.opa.ac.rna$log2FoldChange <= -1))) + 
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 5, y = 50, label = length(which(nc13.res.opa.ac.rna$padj <= 0.05 & nc13.res.opa.ac.rna$log2FoldChange >= 1))) +
  annotate(geom = 'text', x = 0, y = 49, label = length(which(nc13.res.opa.ac.rna$padj <= 0.05 & abs(nc13.res.opa.ac.rna$log2FoldChange) < 1)))
#dev.off()
```

```{r }
  theme_clean() + theme(legend.position = "none")+
  theme(
   plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(title = 'opaKD vs opanoKD DA peaks at NC13')

# Print the plot with annotated counts
nc13.opaKD.opanoKD.vol.atac  + 
  annotate(geom = "text", x = -4, y = 28, label = length(which(nc13.res.opaKD.opanoKD.atac$padj <= 0.05 & nc13.res.opaKD.opanoKD.atac$log2FoldChange <= -1))) + 
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 4, y = 28, label = length(which(nc13.res.opaKD.opanoKD.atac$padj <= 0.05 & nc13.res.opaKD.opanoKD.atac$log2FoldChange >= 1))) +
  annotate(geom = 'text', x = 0, y = 27, label = length(which(nc13.res.opaKD.opanoKD.atac$padj <= 0.05 & abs(nc13.res.opaKD.opanoKD.atac$log2FoldChange) < 1)))
#dev.off()
```



##### NC13 opanoKD vs alignment DA peaks

```{r}
nc13.res.opanoKD.ac.atac <- as.data.frame(results(nc13.atac.dds, contrast = c("genotype", "noKD", "ac"), independentFiltering = FALSE))
# Add Sig, Change, and peak.name columns
nc13.res.opanoKD.ac.atac <- nc13.res.opanoKD.ac.atac%>% 
  mutate(Sig = if_else((padj <= 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >= 1), TRUE, FALSE)) %>% 
  mutate(Change = case_when(
    is.na(log2FoldChange) == TRUE | Sig == FALSE ~ "NA",
    log2FoldChange < 0 ~ "DOWN",
    log2FoldChange > 0 ~ "UP"
  )) %>%mutate(peak.name = rownames(.))

```

Add a column geneId with the nearby gene.

```{r }
   plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
```

## 5. MEME opa DA peaks  


We will use MEME to identify motifs in Cal-opa sensitive peaks.

MEME will be performed on all Cal-opa sensitive peaks, Cal-opa sensitive peaks that lose accessibility and Cal-opa sensitive peaks that gain accessibility. Data will be combined for NC12 and NC13.

Get the names of DA peaks for each stage.
```{r}
nc12.daps.up <- nc12.res.opa.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP") %>% rownames()
nc12.daps.up.IC<-nc12.res.opa.dsred.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP") %>% rownames()
#nc12.daps.up


nc12.daps.down <- nc12.res.opa.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()
nc12.daps.down.IC<-nc12.res.opa.dsred.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()
#nc12.daps.down
```

```{r}
nc13.daps.up <- nc13.res.opa.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP") %>% rownames()
nc13.daps.up.IC<-nc13.res.opaKD.dsred.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP") %>% rownames()
#nc13.daps.up


nc13.daps.down <- nc13.res.opa.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()
nc13.daps.down.IC<-nc13.res.opaKD.dsred.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()
#nc13.daps.down
```

Combine NC12 and NC13 DAPs UP or DOWN. Combine all DAPs UP and DOWN. 
```{r}
# remove any duplicates using unique

opa.daps.up <- unique(c(nc12.daps.up,nc13.daps.up)) 

opa.daps.down <- unique(c(nc12.daps.down,nc13.daps.down))

opa.daps.all <- c(opa.daps.up,opa.daps.down)

opa.daps.up.IC<-unique(c(nc12.daps.up.IC,nc13.daps.up.IC)) 
opa.daps.down.IC<-unique(c(nc12.daps.down.IC,nc13.daps.down.IC)) 
```

get all background peaks

```{r}
nc13.opaKD.ac.daps.BG<-nc13.res.opa.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == FALSE ) %>% rownames()
nc13.opanoKD.ac.daps.BG<-nc13.res.opanoKD.ac.atac  %>% filter(.,Sig == FALSE ) %>% rownames()
nc13.opaKD.opanoKD.daps.BG<-nc13.res.opaKD.opanoKD.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == FALSE ) %>% rownames()
nc13.opaKD.dsred.daps.BG<-nc13.res.opaKD.dsred.atac%>% filter(.,Sig == FALSE ) %>% rownames()
nc12.opaKD.ac.daps.BG<-nc12.res.opa.ac.atac%>% filter(.,Sig == FALSE ) %>% rownames()
nc12.opaKD.dsred.daps.BG<-nc12.res.opa.dsred.atac%>% filter(.,Sig == FALSE ) %>% rownames()

opa.daps.all.BG<-common_names <- Reduce(intersect, list(nc13.opaKD.ac.daps.BG,nc13.opanoKD.ac.daps.BG, nc13.opaKD.opanoKD.daps.BG,nc13.opaKD.dsred.daps.BG, nc12.opaKD.dsred.daps.BG,nc12.opaKD.ac.daps.BG))

```



Get sequences for each peak group using the get.my.seqs function.
```{r eval=FALSE}
# dir for output
sequence.output.directory<-"../MEME"

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% opa.daps.all.BG], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "opa-daps-bg")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% opa.daps.down], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "opa-daps-down")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% opa.daps.up], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "opa-daps-up")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% opa.daps.all], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "opa-daps-all")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% opa.daps.down.IC],dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "opa-daps-down-IC")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% opa.daps.up.IC],dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "opa-daps-up-IC")

```


We identify an Opa motif enriched in Cal-opa sensitive peaks.

Below we will identify peaks with the Opa motif derived from MEME  (Opa PWM 2)

The Opa motif will be searched in peaks as done in previous sections.

#### Find Opa PWM 2 

Read in the frequency matrix from MEME. 
```{r}

opaPWM2 <- as.matrix(read.table("../PWMs/opa_meme_motif_dis.txt", header = FALSE, sep ="\t"))

colnames(opaPWM2) <- c("A","C","G","T")

topaPWM2 <- t(opaPWM2)
seqLogo(topaPWM2)
```

```{r}
# trim low information positions
opaPWM2 <- opaPWM2[3:13,]
topaPWM2 <- t(opaPWM2)
seqLogo(topaPWM2)
```

Save PWM.
```{r eval=FALSE}
pdf(file = "../Plots/opa-meme.pdf", width = 6,height = 5)

seqLogo(topaPWM2)

dev.off()
```

Reverse complement Opa PWM 2
```{r}
topaPWM2RevCom <- t(reverseComplement(opaPWM2))
seqLogo(topaPWM2RevCom)
```

Save PWM.
```{r eval=FALSE}
pdf(file = "../Plots/opa-meme-revcom.pdf", width = 6,height = 5)

seqLogo(topaPWM2RevCom)

dev.off()
```


(We will save time and skip this part, the updated motif table can be found in ./WT_timecourse/motif-table.txt) 

Opa PWM 2 in peaks. We will search both strands

```{r eval=FALSE}
opa.peak.2 <- lapply(seq.peaks, function(x){
  matchPWM(topaPWM2, subject = x, min.score = "80%",with.score = TRUE)
})

opa.peak.rc.2 <- lapply(seq.peaks, function(x){
  matchPWM(topaPWM2RevCom, subject = x, min.score = "80%",with.score = TRUE)
})
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
# peaks with at least one match will have a length greater than 0

n.opa.peak.2 <- opa.peak.2[lengths(opa.peak.2) > 0] 

n.opa.peak.rc.2 <- opa.peak.rc.2[lengths(opa.peak.rc.2) > 0] 
```


```{r eval=FALSE}
paste0("percent of peaks with an opa MEME motif ",
       round(length(unique(c(names(n.opa.peak.2),names(n.opa.peak.rc.2))))/(length(peaks.32157))*100,1),"%")


```

```{r eval=FALSE}
paste0("percent of peaks with an opa motif ",
       round(length(unique(c(names(n.opa.peak),names(n.opa.peak.rc),names(n.opa.peak.2),names(n.opa.peak.rc.2))))/(length(peaks.32157))*100,1),"%")
```

Update the motif table
```{r eval=FALSE}
opa.peaks.2.l <- names(peaks.32157) %in% names(n.opa.peak.2)
opa.peaks.rc.2.l <- names(peaks.32157) %in% names(n.opa.peak.rc.2)
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
motif.table <- data.frame(motif.table,
           opa.sites.2 = opa.peaks.2.l,
           opa.sites.rc.2 = opa.peaks.rc.2.l)


#head(motif.table)
```

SAVE updated motif table.
```{r eval=FALSE}
write.table(motif.table,file = "../WT_timecourse/motif-table.txt", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE)
```


## 6. Identifying Cal-opa targets

Starting with NC12 

### NC12

##### NC12 high-level observations 

Before we get to the targets. We will report some high-level observations.

For these observations the tables characterizing peaks (e.g. genomic.feature.peaks, motif.table)  produced in previous sections will be used. Dplyr will be used to merge, filter and manipulate dfs.

Below is the % of DA peaks whose accessibility decreases or increases (DA peaks DOWN or DA peaks UP).

```{r}
motif.table<-read_delim("../WT_timecourse/motif-table.txt")
```

```{r}
nc12.res.opa.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE) %>% 
  count(.,Change) %>%
  mutate(percent = round((n / sum(n)) * 100,1)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(percent))
```



Below is the % of DA peaks segmented by genomic feature (exon, intron, exon-intron, promoter, or intergenic).
```{r}
nc12.res.opa.ac.atac  %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=genomic.feature.peaks, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE)  %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=motif.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>% 
  #arrange(original.row) %>%
  filter(.,Sig == TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(has.opa.motif = if_else((opa.sites==TRUE | opa.sites.rc == TRUE | opa.sites.2 == TRUE | opa.sites.rc.2),TRUE,FALSE)) %>% 
  count(genomic.feature) %>%
  mutate(percent = round((n / sum(n)) * 100,1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(percent))
```

Below is the % of DA peaks segmented by change and genomic feature (exon, intron, exon-intron, promoter, or intergenic).
```{r}
nc12.res.opa.ac.atac  %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=genomic.feature.peaks, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE)  %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=motif.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>% 
  #arrange(original.row) %>%
  filter(.,Sig == TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(has.opa.motif = if_else((opa.sites==TRUE | opa.sites.rc == TRUE | opa.sites.2 == TRUE | opa.sites.rc.2),TRUE,FALSE)) %>% 
  group_by(Change) %>%
  count(genomic.feature) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(percent = round((n / sum(n)) * 100,1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(percent))



```

Below is the % of DA peaks that fall into a dynamic/non dynamic group segmented by change. Write to df.
```{r}
nc12.opa.daps.dyn <- nc12.res.opa.ac.atac %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=patterns.group.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>%
  merge(x=.,y=peaks.open.by.stage, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(class = case_when(
  group.1 == TRUE ~ "group.1",
  group.2 == TRUE ~ "group.2",
  group.3 == TRUE ~ "group.3",
  group.4 == TRUE ~ "group.4",
  group.5 == TRUE ~ "group.5",
  group.6 == TRUE ~ "group.6",
  group.7 == TRUE ~ "group.7",
  group.8 == TRUE ~ "group.8",
  group.9 == TRUE ~ "group.9",
  group.10 == TRUE ~ "group.10",
  group.11 == TRUE ~ "group.11",
  group.12 == TRUE ~ "group.12",
  group.13 == TRUE ~ "group.13",
  group.14 == TRUE ~ "group.14",
  group.15 == TRUE ~ "group.15",
  group.16 == TRUE ~ "group.16",
  group.17 == TRUE ~ "group.17",
  group.18 == TRUE ~ "group.18",
  group.19 == TRUE ~ "group.19",
  group.20 == TRUE ~ "group.20",
  group.21 == TRUE ~ "group.21",
  dynamic.peak == TRUE & dynamic.in.class == FALSE ~ "dynamic not in group",
  dynamic.peak == FALSE & dynamic.in.class == FALSE ~ "not dynamic not in group")) %>%
  filter(.,Sig ==TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(.,Change) %>%
  count(.,class) %>%
  mutate(percent = round((n / sum(n)) * 100,1)) 


```


Now we want to identify TFs that are differentially expressed upon Cal-opa depletion and whose loci contain Cal-opa sensitive peaks.

We will make a df of DEGs and the corresponding peaks in their loci. We will add other information (e.g. from the results of the DE analysis) to this df including if the peak is DA in Cal-opa KD embryos and if the peak contains Opa motifs.

First for each DEG a 40 Kb gene region will be defined. 
```{r}
nc12.degs <- nc12.res.opa.ac.rna %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE) %>% rownames() # get the names of the degs

nc12.deg.regions <- resize(transcripts.by.gene[names(transcripts.by.gene) %in% nc12.degs],width = 40000,fix = "center") # define a gene region of 40Kb for degs
```

Now for each gene find peaks within its locus.  Make a new df with the gene name (gene.locus) and name of peak (peak.name).
```{r}
nc12.deg.regions.peaks <- as.data.frame(findOverlaps(query = peaks.32157,subject = nc12.deg.regions,type="any")) # find overlaps of peaks in deg regions, return a df

# update the df so that it has the gene and the peak name
nc12.deg.regions.peaks <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>%
mutate(.,gene.locus=names(nc12.deg.regions[subjectHits]),peak.name = names(peaks.32157[queryHits]))

head(nc12.deg.regions.peaks)
```

```{r}
all(unique(nc12.deg.regions.peaks$gene.locus) %in% nc12.degs) # check all degs have at least one peak
```

We will integrate the results of the DE ATAC-seq analysis. We will add a column, "DA", indicating if a peak has undergone a significant change in accessibility. We will add a column, "Change.peak", indicating if the change in accessibility was up or down.
```{r}
nc12.deg.regions.peaks <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% 
  merge(., y=nc12.res.opa.ac.atac, by.x ="peak.name", by.y ="peak.name", all.x = TRUE)  %>% select(-c(baseMean,log2FoldChange,lfcSE,stat,pvalue,padj)) %>% 
  rename(DA=Sig,Change.peak=Change) %>% 
  relocate(peak.name, .after=gene.locus) 
```

We will integrate the motif data (in motif.table). We will add a column, “has.opa.motif”, which is TRUE if a peak has a motif matching an Opa PWM (using the Dme PWM or MEME derived Opa PWM). 
```{r}
nc12.deg.regions.peaks <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>%
  merge(x=.,y=motif.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(has.opa.motif = if_else((opa.sites==TRUE | opa.sites.rc == TRUE | opa.sites.2 == TRUE | opa.sites.rc.2),TRUE,FALSE)) %>% 
  select(-c(opa.sites,opa.sites.rc,zld.sites,zld.sites.rc,opa.sites.2,opa.sites.rc.2))

head(nc12.deg.regions.peaks)
```

Integrate the genomic feature data (genomic.feature.peaks table), add the “genomic.region” from this df which indicates if a peak is either an exon, intron, exon-intron, promoter, or intergenic.
```{r}
nc12.deg.regions.peaks <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% 
  merge(x=., y=genomic.feature.peaks, by.x="peak.name", by.y="peak.name", all.x = TRUE) %>% select(-c(intergenic,promoter,intron,exon,original.row))

head(nc12.deg.regions.peaks)
```

Add a column to indicate if the change in the gene’s expression was up or down.
```{r}
nc12.deg.regions.peaks <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% 
  merge( x=., y=nc12.res.opa.ac.rna, by.x="gene.locus",by.y = "gene.locus", all.x = TRUE)  %>% select(-c(baseMean,log2FoldChange,lfcSE,stat,pvalue,padj))

head(nc12.deg.regions.peaks)
```


Finally, we will integrate the annotation information for these genes. Later we want to filter for COG and GO terms matching transcription/transcription factor.

Use the gene name (gene.locus) to find a match in the annotation data (contained in all.annote.data). The ID match contains the COG,GO information, While the Parent match has the Dme homolog and flybase information. Note: a gene may have more than one entry (corresponding to multiple transcripts). Note: The annotation gff3 was manually corrected for two sets of paralogs. For these genes their "gene.locus" is simplified to their pre-manually correction name in this loop. This is okay because we are only pulling meta information for the gene not gene coordinates.

For each gene get the desired information for the match in the parent or ID column.   
```{r}
for (i in 1:nrow(nc12.deg.regions.peaks)){
        goi <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks$gene.locus[i]
        if(goi == "evm.TU.scaffold_3.2548a" | goi == "evm.TU.scaffold_3.2548b"){
                goi <- "evm.TU.scaffold_3.2548"}else{
                  if(goi == "evm.TU.scaffold_4.40a" | goi == "evm.TU.scaffold_4.40b"){ 
                          goi <- "evm.TU.scaffold_4.40"}else{
                            goi <- goi}}
        # get the index of the match to deg name to the parent column
        index.parent <- which(all.annote.data$Parent == goi)[1]
        
        # repeat for the ID column, which has the GO and COG information
        index.ID <- which(all.annote.data$ID == goi)[1]
        
        
        # from the matched parent or row get information of interest
        
        nc12.deg.regions.peaks$Parent[i] <- all.annote.data$Parent[index.parent]
        nc12.deg.regions.peaks$ID[i] <- all.annote.data$ID[index.ID]
        
        # from ID
        nc12.deg.regions.peaks$Name[i] <- all.annote.data$Name[index.ID]
        nc12.deg.regions.peaks$Preferred_name[i] <- all.annote.data$Preferred_name[index.ID]
        nc12.deg.regions.peaks$GOs[i] <- all.annote.data$GOs[index.ID]
        nc12.deg.regions.peaks$COG_category[i] <- all.annote.data$COG_category[index.ID]
        
         # from parent 
        nc12.deg.regions.peaks$dme.hit[i] <- all.annote.data$dme.hits[index.parent]
        nc12.deg.regions.peaks$flybase.id[i] <- all.annote.data$flybase.id[index.parent]
  
  }


```

```{r}
head(nc12.deg.regions.peaks)
```



Now that the necessary data is aggregated we can answer some questions. 


##### DE TFs at NC12

How many DEGs are TFs?

Below returns a table of the DE TFs; each gene name, flybase ID (if a Dme homolog was identified), and the number of peaks within its loci.
```{r}
nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% 
  filter(grepl("K",COG_category) | grepl("GO:0003700",GOs)) %>% 
  group_by(.,gene.locus) %>% 
  count(flybase.id) 
```

Write DE TFs to a df. Note there will be multiple entries (rows) for TFs with more than one peak in its locus.  A new row is generated for each peak a TF has.  
```{r}
nc12.deg.tfs <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% filter(grepl("K",COG_category) | grepl("GO:0003700",GOs)) 
```

Below shows if the change in expression for a DE TF was up or down.
```{r}
nc12.deg.tfs %>%
  distinct(.,Sig,Change,gene.locus) 
```


##### DE TFs with Opa positive ATAC-seq peaks 

Lets determine how many DE TFs have at least one ATAC-seq peak with an Opa motif. This TFs are putative direct targets. 

Below returns a table of the DE TFs; each gene name, flybase ID (if a Dme homolog was identified), and the number of Opa motif positive peaks within its loci.
```{r}
nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% filter(grepl("K",COG_category) | grepl("GO:0003700",GOs)) %>% 
  filter(has.opa.motif ==TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(.,gene.locus) %>% 
  count(flybase.id)  
```

Write to a df.
```{r}
nc12.deg.tfs.w.opa <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% 
  filter(grepl("K",COG_category) | grepl("GO:0003700",GOs)) %>% 
  filter(has.opa.motif ==TRUE) 
```



##### DE TFs with Cal-Opa sensitive peaks

Lets identify DE TFs that have at least one Cal-opa sensitive peak.  

Below returns a table of the DE TFs; each gene name, flybase ID (if a Dme homolog was identified), and the number of Cal-opa sensitive peak (DAPs) within its loci.

We identify hbn (evm.TU.scaffold_4.1647), slp1 (evm.TU.scaffold_5.983), slp2 (evm.TU.scaffold_5.985) and opa (evm.TU.scaffold_7.878).
```{r}
nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% filter(grepl("K",COG_category) | grepl("GO:0003700",GOs)) %>% 
  filter(.,DA == TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(.,gene.locus) %>% 
  count(flybase.id)  
```

Write to a df.
```{r}
nc12.deg.tfs.w.dap <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% filter(grepl("K",COG_category) | grepl("GO:0003700",GOs)) %>% 
  filter(.,DA == TRUE)

```



##### DE TFs with Cal-Opa sensitive peaks with an Opa motif.  (AKA key targets)


Lets identify DE TFs that have at least one Opa motif positive Cal-opa sensitive peak.  

Below returns a table of the DE TFs; each gene name, flybase ID (if a Dme homolog was identified), and the number of Opa motif positive Cal-opa sensitive peak (Opa+ DAPs) within its loci.

We identify hbn (evm.TU.scaffold_4.1647), slp1 (evm.TU.scaffold_5.983), slp2 (evm.TU.scaffold_5.985) and opa (evm.TU.scaffold_7.878).
```{r}
nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% filter(grepl("K",COG_category) | grepl("GO:0003700",GOs)) %>% 
  filter(has.opa.motif ==TRUE & DA == TRUE) %>% 
  group_by(.,gene.locus) %>% 
  count(flybase.id)  
```

Write to a df.
```{r}
nc12.deg.tfs.w.dap.w.opa <- nc12.deg.regions.peaks %>% 
  filter(grepl("K",COG_category) | grepl("GO:0003700",GOs)) %>% 
  filter(has.opa.motif ==TRUE & DA == TRUE)
```

####  NC12 opa vs injection control (dsred) comparison

To test the robustness of this result we will identify what DE TFs potentially targeted by Cal-Opa directly and DE TFs with Cal-opa sensitive peaks that are also recovered when opa is compared to the injection control (dsred).

Get results for opa vs dsred comparison for both the RNA-seq and ATAC-seq DESeq2 analysis.

To either the RNA or ATAC results...

Add a column Add a column, "Sig", indicating if a gene/peak is significantly differential expressed/accessible.

Add a column, "gene.locus", with the gene name.  

Add a column, "peak.name", with the peak name.

RNA
```{r}
nc12.res.opa.dsred.rna <- as.data.frame(results(nc12.rna.dds, contrast = c("genotype", "opa", "dsred"), independentFiltering = FALSE))

nc12.res.opa.dsred.rna  <- nc12.res.opa.dsred.rna %>% mutate(.,Sig = if_else((padj <= 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >=1),TRUE,FALSE))

nc12.res.opa.dsred.rna <- nc12.res.opa.dsred.rna %>% mutate(gene.locus = rownames(.))

```

ATAC
```{r}
nc12.res.opa.dsred.atac <- as.data.frame(results(nc12.atac.dds, contrast = c("genotype", "opa", "dsred"), independentFiltering = FALSE))

nc12.res.opa.dsred.atac  <- nc12.res.opa.dsred.atac %>% mutate(.,Sig = if_else((padj <= 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >=1),TRUE,FALSE))

nc12.res.opa.dsred.atac <- nc12.res.opa.dsred.atac %>% mutate(peak.name = rownames(.))
```



###### What putative direct targets (DE TFs with Opa positive ATAC-seq peaks ) are also significant when opa is compared to the injection control (dsred)?

DE TFs with Opa positive ATAC-seq peaks are in the df "nc12.deg.tfs.w.opa".

We will add columns to the df "nc12.deg.tfs.w.opa" containing the results of the opa vs injection control (dsred) comparison. We will make new columns "LFC.opa.v.dsred" and "padj.opa.v.dsred" containing the log2FC and adjusted p-value from this comparison. We will also add a column "Sig.opa.v.dsred", indicating if a TF's change in expression was significant. This will produce a new table "nc12.deg.tfs.w.opa.opa.v.dsred".

```{r}
nc12.deg.tfs.w.opa.opa.v.dsred <- nc12.deg.tfs.w.opa  %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=nc12.res.opa.dsred.rna,by = "gene.locus", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  rename(., LFC.opa.v.dsred = log2FoldChange,
         padj.opa.v.dsred = padj,
         Sig.opa.v.dsred = Sig.y) %>% 
  select(., -c(baseMean,lfcSE,stat,pvalue)) 

```

Filter this table for TFs DE in opa vs injection control (dsred). 

We find that hbn, slp1, slp2 and opa are significantly differentially expressed. 

Other TFs do not meet the significance threshold.
```{r}
nc12.deg.tfs.w.opa.opa.v.dsred  %>% select(c(gene.locus,LFC.opa.v.dsred,padj.opa.v.dsred,Sig.opa.v.dsred,has.opa.motif)) %>% distinct(.) %>% filter(., Sig.opa.v.dsred == TRUE)

```



###### What DE TFs with Cal-Opa sensitive peaks are also significant when opa is compared to the injection control (dsred)?

DE TFs with Cal-Opa sensitive peaks are in the df "nc12.deg.tfs.w.dap".

We will add columns to the df "nc12.deg.tfs.w.dap" containing the results of the opa vs injection control (dsred) comparison. We will make new columns "LFC.opa.v.dsred" and "padj.opa.v.dsred" containing the log2FC an adjusted p-value from this comparison. We will also add acolumn "Sig.opa.v.dsred", indicating if peaks change in accessibility was significant. This will produce a new table "nc12.deg.tfs.w.dap.opa.v.dsred".


```{r}
nc12.deg.tfs.w.dap.opa.v.dsred <- nc12.deg.tfs.w.dap %>%
  merge(x=.,y=nc12.res.opa.dsred.atac,by = "peak.name", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  rename(., LFC.opa.v.dsred = log2FoldChange,
         padj.opa.v.dsred = padj,
         Sig.opa.v.dsred = Sig.y) %>% 
  select(., -c(baseMean,lfcSE,stat,pvalue)) 

```



Peaks at the loci of hbn  (scaffold_4:18077983-18078654,scaffold_4:18079790-18080495), slp1  (scaffold_5:23577384-23577708) and opa (scaffold_7:16236995-16237127) are significantly differentially accessible. 

Other peaks do not meet the significance threshold for significance. 

```{r}
nc12.deg.tfs.w.dap.opa.v.dsred  %>% select(c(gene.locus,peak.name,has.opa.motif,LFC.opa.v.dsred,padj.opa.v.dsred,Sig.opa.v.dsred)) %>% filter(.,Sig.opa.v.dsred ==TRUE)
```
