Now we want to identify TFs that are differentially expressed upon Cal-opa depletion and whose loci contain Cal-opa sensitive peaks.

We will make a df of DEGs and the corresponding peaks in their loci. We will add other information (e.g. from the results of the DE analysis) to this df including if the peak is DA in Cal-opa KD embryos and if the peak contains Opa motifs.

```{r}
nc13.degs <- nc13.res.opa.ac.rna %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE) %>% rownames() # get the names of the degs
nc13.deg.regions <- resize(transcripts.by.gene[names(transcripts.by.gene) %in% nc13.degs],width = 40000,fix = "center") # define a gene region of 40Kb for degs
```

Now for each gene find peaks within its locus.  Make a new df with the gene name (gene.locus) and name of peak (peak.name).
```{r}
nc13.deg.regions.peaks <- as.data.frame(findOverlaps(query = peaks.32157,subject = nc13.deg.regions,type="any")) # find overlaps of peaks in deg regions, return a df

# update the data frame so that it has the deg and the peak name
nc13.deg.regions.peaks <- nc13.deg.regions.peaks %>%
mutate(.,gene.locus=names(nc13.deg.regions[subjectHits]),peak.name = names(peaks.32157[queryHits]))

head(nc13.deg.regions.peaks)

```

```{r}
all(unique(nc13.deg.regions.peaks$gene.locus) %in% nc13.degs) # check that all degs have at least one peak
```

We will integrate the results of the DE ATAC-seq analysis. We will add a column, "DA", indicating if a peak has undergone a significant change in accessibility. We will add a column, "Change.peak", indicating if the change in accessibility was up or down.
```{r}
nc13.deg.regions.peaks <- nc13.deg.regions.peaks %>% 
  merge(., y=nc13.res.opa.ac.atac, by.x ="peak.name", by.y ="peak.name", all.x = TRUE) %>% select(-c(baseMean,log2FoldChange,lfcSE,stat,pvalue,padj)) %>% 
  rename(DA=Sig,Change.peak=Change) %>% 
  relocate(peak.name, .after=gene.locus) 

```

We will integrate the motif data (in motif.table). We will add a column, “has.opa.motif”, which is TRUE if a peak has a motif matching an Opa PWM (using the Dme PWM or MEME derived Opa PWM). 
```{r}
nc13.deg.regions.peaks <- nc13.deg.regions.peaks %>%
  merge(x=.,y=motif.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(has.opa.motif = if_else((opa.sites==TRUE | opa.sites.rc == TRUE | opa.sites.2 == TRUE | opa.sites.rc.2),TRUE,FALSE)) %>% 
  select(-c(opa.sites,opa.sites.rc,zld.sites,zld.sites.rc,opa.sites.2,opa.sites.rc.2))


head(nc13.deg.regions.peaks)

```

Integrate the genomic feature data (genomic.feature.peaks table), add the “genomic.region” from this df which indicates if a peak is either an exon, intron, exon-intron, promoter, or intergenic.
```{r}
nc13.deg.regions.peaks <- nc13.deg.regions.peaks %>% 
  merge(x=., y=genomic.feature.peaks, by.x="peak.name", by.y="peak.name", all.x = TRUE) %>% select(-c(intergenic,promoter,intron,exon,original.row))
```

Add a column to indicate if the change in the gene’s expression was up or down.
```{r}
nc13.deg.regions.peaks <- nc13.deg.regions.peaks %>% merge( x=., y=nc13.res.opa.ac.rna, by.x="gene.locus",by.y = "gene.locus", all.x = TRUE)  %>% select(-c(baseMean,log2FoldChange,lfcSE,stat,pvalue,padj))
```

Finally, we will integrate the annotation information for these genes. Later we want to filter for COG and GO terms matching transcription/transcription factor.
```{r}
# For each gene get the desired information for the match in the parent or ID column
for (i in 1:nrow(nc13.deg.regions.peaks)){
        goi <- nc13.deg.regions.peaks$gene.locus[i]
        if(goi == "evm.TU.scaffold_3.2548a" | goi == "evm.TU.scaffold_3.2548b"){
                goi <- "evm.TU.scaffold_3.2548"}else{
                  if(goi == "evm.TU.scaffold_4.40a" | goi == "evm.TU.scaffold_4.40b"){ 
                          goi <- "evm.TU.scaffold_4.40"}else{
                            goi <- goi}}
        # get the index of the match to deg name to the parent column
        index.parent <- which(all.annote.data$Parent == goi)[1]
        
        # repeat for the ID column, which has the GO and COG information
        index.ID <- which(all.annote.data$ID == goi)[1]
        
        
        # from the matched parent or row get information of interest
        
        nc13.deg.regions.peaks$Parent[i] <- all.annote.data$Parent[index.parent]
        nc13.deg.regions.peaks$ID[i] <- all.annote.data$ID[index.ID]
        
        # from ID
        nc13.deg.regions.peaks$Name[i] <- all.annote.data$Name[index.ID]
        nc13.deg.regions.peaks$Preferred_name[i] <- all.annote.data$Preferred_name[index.ID]
        nc13.deg.regions.peaks$GOs[i] <- all.annote.data$GOs[index.ID]
        nc13.deg.regions.peaks$COG_category[i] <- all.annote.data$COG_category[index.ID]
        
         # from parent 
        nc13.deg.regions.peaks$dme.hit[i] <- all.annote.data$dme.hits[index.parent]
        nc13.deg.regions.peaks$flybase.id[i] <- all.annote.data$flybase.id[index.parent]
 
  }

```


####  NC13 opa vs injection control (dsred) comparison

To test the robustness of this result we will identify what DE TFs potentially targeted by Cal-Opa directly and DE TFs with Cal-opa sensitive peaks that are also recovered when opa is compared to the injection control (dsred).

Get results for opa vs dsred for both the RNA-seq and ATAC-seq DESeq2 analysis.

To either the RNA or ATAC results...

Add a column Add a column, "Sig", indicating if a gene/peak is significantly differential expressed/accessible.

Add a column, "gene.locus", with the gene name.  

Add a column, "peak.name", with the peak name.

RNA
```{r}
nc13.res.opa.dsred.rna <- as.data.frame(results(nc13.rna.dds, contrast = c("genotype", "opa", "dsred"), independentFiltering = FALSE))

nc13.res.opa.dsred.rna  <- nc13.res.opa.dsred.rna %>% mutate(.,Sig = if_else((padj <= 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >=1),TRUE,FALSE))

nc13.res.opa.dsred.rna <- nc13.res.opa.dsred.rna %>% mutate(gene.locus = rownames(.))
```

ATAC
```{r}
nc13.res.opa.dsred.atac <- as.data.frame(results(nc13.atac.dds, contrast = c("genotype", "opa", "dsred"), independentFiltering = FALSE))

nc13.res.opa.dsred.atac  <- nc13.res.opa.dsred.atac %>% mutate(.,Sig = if_else((padj <= 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >=1),TRUE,FALSE))

nc13.res.opa.dsred.atac <- nc13.res.opa.dsred.atac %>% mutate(peak.name = rownames(.))

```



###### What putative direct targets (DE TFs with Opa positive ATAC-seq peaks ) are also significant when opa is compared to the injection control (dsred)?

DE TFs with Opa positive ATAC-seq peaks are in the df "nc13.deg.tfs.w.opa".

We will add columns to the df "nc13.deg.tfs.w.opa" containing the results of the opa vs injection control (dsred) comparison. We will make new columns "LFC.opa.v.dsred" and "padj.opa.v.dsred" containing the log2FC an adjusted p-value from this comparison. We will also add a column "Sig.opa.v.dsred", indicating if a TF’s change in expression was significant. This will produce a new table "nc13.deg.tfs.w.opa.opa.v.dsred".

```{r}
nc13.deg.tfs.w.opa.opa.v.dsred <- nc13.deg.tfs.w.opa  %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=nc13.res.opa.dsred.rna,by = "gene.locus", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  rename(., LFC.opa.v.dsred = log2FoldChange,
         padj.opa.v.dsred = padj,
         Sig.opa.v.dsred = Sig.y) %>% 
  select(., -c(baseMean,lfcSE,stat,pvalue)) 

```


Filter this table for TFs DE in opa vs injection control (dsred). 

hbn, slp1, slp2 and evm.TU.scaffold_7.53	are significantly differentially expressed. 

Other TFs do not meet the significance threshold.
```{r}
nc13.deg.tfs.w.opa.opa.v.dsred  %>% 
  select(c(gene.locus,flybase.id,LFC.opa.v.dsred,padj.opa.v.dsred,Sig.opa.v.dsred,has.opa.motif,flybase.id)) %>% 
  distinct(.) %>% filter(Sig.opa.v.dsred == TRUE)
```

## 7. Bicoid targets in Cal-opa

Bcd is required to drive anterior expression of segmentation genes and  to establish the accessibility of a set of anterior enhancers. Bcd sensitive enhancers have been described in the Hannon et al 2017 elife study in Drosophila.

We will check if Cal-opa affects Bcd targets and other developmental genes of interest (goi). Some of these genes have already come up at NC12 and/or NC13 as a Cal-opa direct or indirect target either transcriptionally or at the level of chromatin accessibility.

Read in df with gois
```{r}
goi.df <- read_xlsx("../opaKD/cal-dev-gois.xlsx")

goi.df
```


First for each goi a 40 Kb gene region will be defined. 
```{r}
goi.regions <- resize(calbi.genes[names(calbi.genes) %in% goi.df$gene.locus],width = 40000,fix = "center")

head(goi.regions)
```


Now for each gene find peaks within its locus.  Make a new df with the gene name (gene.locus) and name of peak (peak.name).
```{r}
nc12.goi.regions.peaks <- as.data.frame(findOverlaps(query = peaks.32157,subject = goi.regions,type="any")) # find overlaps of peaks in goi regions, return a df

# update the data frame so that it has the goi and the peak name
# add the common gene name
nc12.goi.regions.peaks <- nc12.goi.regions.peaks %>%
mutate(.,gene.locus=names(goi.regions[subjectHits]),peak.name = names(peaks.32157[queryHits])) %>% merge(x=., y=goi.df, by.x ="gene.locus", by.y = "gene.locus",all.x = TRUE)

head(nc12.goi.regions.peaks)
```


```{r}
all(unique(nc12.goi.regions.peaks$gene.locus) %in% goi.df$gene.locus) # check all degs have at least one peak
```


We will integrate the results of the DE ATAC-seq analysis. We will add a column, "DA", indicating if a peak has undergone a significant change in accessibility. We will add a column, "Change.peak", indicating if the change in accessibility was up or down. We will integrate the results of the DE RNA-seq analysis. We will add a column, "Sig.gene", indicating if a gene is significantly differential expressed. We will add a column "Change.gene" ,indicating if the change in expression was up or down. 

We will integrate the motif data (in motif.table). We will add a column, “has.opa.motif”, which is TRUE if a peak has a motif matching an Opa PWM (using the Dme PWM or MEME derived Opa PWM). We will add a column, “has.zld.motif”, which is TRUE if a peak has a motif matching the Zld PWM. 

We will integrate the genomic feature data (genomic.feature.peaks table), add the “genomic.region” from this df which indicates if a peak is either an exon, intron, exon-intron, promoter, or intergenic. We will integrate the dynamic/non dynamic peak classification (in patterns.group.table).

```{r}
nc12.goi.regions.peaks <- nc12.goi.regions.peaks  %>% 
  merge(., y=nc12.res.opa.ac.rna, by.x ="gene.locus", by.y ="gene.locus", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  select(-c(lfcSE,stat,pvalue,row.name)) %>%
  rename(baseMean.gene=baseMean,LFC.gene=log2FoldChange,padj.gene=padj,Sig.gene=Sig,Change.gene=Change) %>% 
  merge(., y=nc12.res.opa.ac.atac, by.x ="peak.name", by.y ="peak.name", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  select(-c(baseMean,lfcSE,stat,pvalue,row.name)) %>%
  rename(DA=Sig,Change.peak=Change,LFC.peak=log2FoldChange,padj.peak=padj) %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=genomic.feature.peaks, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=motif.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=patterns.group.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(has.opa.motif = if_else((opa.sites==TRUE | opa.sites.rc == TRUE | opa.sites.2 == TRUE | opa.sites.rc.2),TRUE,FALSE)) %>%
  mutate(has.zld.motif = if_else((zld.sites ==TRUE | zld.sites.rc == TRUE ),TRUE,FALSE)) %>%
  select(-c(intergenic,promoter,intron,exon,original.row,opa.sites,opa.sites.rc,opa.sites.rc,opa.sites.rc,zld.sites,zld.sites.rc,opa.sites.2,opa.sites.rc.2))  %>% 
  relocate(c(has.opa.motif,has.zld.motif), .after=genomic.feature) %>% 
  relocate(c(non.dynamic.peak,dynamic.peak,dynamic.in.class),.after=has.zld.motif) %>% 
  relocate(peak.name, .after=Change.gene)

head(nc12.goi.regions.peaks)
```


We will filter for genes that either have a significant change in expression or whose loci contain Cal-opa sensitive ATAC-seq peaks. We will produce a df for each gene.

hbn, slp1, slp2 and opa are differentially expressed and contain Opa + Cal-Opa sensitive peaks. slp3 is differentially expressed. No other developmental gois not affected by Cal-opa depletion at NC12. 
```{r}
nc12.goi.regions.peaks %>% 
  filter(.,Sig.gene == TRUE | DA == TRUE) %>% select(gene.locus,cal.name,Sig.gene,Change.gene,DA,Change.peak,has.opa.motif) %>% 
  group_by(gene.locus) %>% group_split()
```


Repeat for NC13.

```{r}
nc13.goi.regions.peaks <- as.data.frame(findOverlaps(query = peaks.32157,subject = goi.regions,type="any")) # find overlaps of peaks in goi regions, return a df

# update the data frame so that it has the goi and the peak name
# add the common gene name
nc13.goi.regions.peaks <- nc13.goi.regions.peaks %>%
mutate(.,gene.locus=names(goi.regions[subjectHits]),peak.name = names(peaks.32157[queryHits])) %>% merge(x=., y=goi.df, by.x ="gene.locus", by.y = "gene.locus",all.x = TRUE)

head(nc13.goi.regions.peaks)
```

```{r}
all(unique(nc13.goi.regions.peaks$gene.locus) %in% goi.df$gene.locus) # check all degs have at least one peak
```


We will integrate the results of the DE ATAC-seq analysis. We will add a column, "DA", indicating if a peak has undergone a significant change in accessibility. We will add a column, "Change.peak", indicating if the change in accessibility was up or down. We will integrate the results of the DE RNA-seq analysis. We will add a column, "Sig.gene", indicating if a gene is significantly differential expressed. We will add a column "Change.gene" ,indicating if the change in expression was up or down. 

We will integrate the motif data (in motif.table). We will add a column, “has.opa.motif”, which is TRUE if a peak has a motif matching an Opa PWM (using the Dme PWM or MEME derived Opa PWM). We will add a column, “has.zld.motif”, which is TRUE if a peak has a motif matching the Zld PWM. 

We will integrate the genomic feature data (genomic.feature.peaks table), add the “genomic.region” from this df which indicates if a peak is either an exon, intron, exon-intron, promoter, or intergenic. We will integrate the dynamic/non dynamic peak classification (in patterns.group.table).

```{r}
nc13.goi.regions.peaks <- nc13.goi.regions.peaks  %>% 
  merge(., y=nc13.res.opa.ac.rna, by.x ="gene.locus", by.y ="gene.locus", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  select(-c(lfcSE,stat,pvalue,row.name)) %>%
  rename(baseMean.gene=baseMean,LFC.gene=log2FoldChange,padj.gene=padj,Sig.gene=Sig,Change.gene=Change) %>% 
  merge(., y=nc13.res.opa.ac.atac, by.x ="peak.name", by.y ="peak.name", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  select(-c(baseMean,lfcSE,stat,pvalue,row.name)) %>%
  rename(DA=Sig,Change.peak=Change,LFC.peak=log2FoldChange,padj.peak=padj) %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=genomic.feature.peaks, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=motif.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=patterns.group.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(has.opa.motif = if_else((opa.sites==TRUE | opa.sites.rc == TRUE | opa.sites.2 == TRUE | opa.sites.rc.2),TRUE,FALSE)) %>%
  mutate(has.zld.motif = if_else((zld.sites ==TRUE | zld.sites.rc == TRUE ),TRUE,FALSE)) %>%
  select(-c(intergenic,promoter,intron,exon,original.row,opa.sites,opa.sites.rc,opa.sites.rc,opa.sites.rc,zld.sites,zld.sites.rc,opa.sites.2,opa.sites.rc.2))  %>% 
  relocate(c(has.opa.motif,has.zld.motif), .after=genomic.feature) %>% 
  relocate(c(non.dynamic.peak,dynamic.peak,dynamic.in.class),.after=has.zld.motif) %>% 
  relocate(peak.name, .after=Change.gene)

head(nc13.goi.regions.peaks)
```



We will filter for genes that either have a significant change in expression or whose loci contain Cal-opa sensitive ATAC-seq peaks. We will produce a df for each gene.

hbn, slp1, slp2, D, Kr and opa are differentially expressed and contain Opa + Cal-Opa sensitive peak(s). slp3 is differentially expressed and contains one Cal-opa sensitive peak, this peak does not have an Opa motif. cnc is not expressed at this stage, its locus has one Cal-opa sensitive peak but the peak does not contain an Opa motif, visual inspection confirms this is a small peak. hb1 and hb2 are differential expressed and have Cal-opa sensitive peaks, however none of the peaks contain Opa motifs. hkb is not expressed at this stage, there is one Cal-opa sensitive peak that contains an Opa motif at its locus. The expression of eve2 is increased, the peaks at it locus are Cal-Opa insensitive. The expression of btd is reduced but does not meet the significance threshold, the btd locus contains one Opa motif positive Cal-opa sensitive peak. The expression of otd1 is significantly reduced and it locus contains two Cal-opa sensitive peaks but the peaks do not contain Opa motifs. 

```{r}
nc13.goi.regions.peaks %>% 
  filter(.,Sig.gene == TRUE | DA == TRUE) %>% 
select(cal.name,gene.locus,peak.name,Sig.gene,Change.gene,DA,Change.peak,has.opa.motif) %>%
  group_by(gene.locus)  %>% 
  group_split(.,)

```

```{r eval=FALSE}
nc13.goi.regions.peaks <- cbind("row.name" =rownames(nc13.goi.regions.peaks),nc13.goi.regions.peaks)

write_xlsx(list("nc12.goi.regions.peaks"=as.data.frame(nc12.goi.regions.peaks),
                "nc13.goi.regions.peaks"=as.data.frame(nc13.goi.regions.peaks)),
```

# Section 3 zld

### Background

ATAC-seq was performed on Cal-zld RNAi  embryos at Late NC14. RNA was isolated from the ATAC preps and made into RNA-seq libraries. Two control groups were collected for these experiments. 1) Wild-type (WT): untreated  embryos. 2) Alignment controls: aligned on the injected slide and not injected. Successful Cal-zld knockdown is determined from the RNA-seq data by a fold change (FC) calculation. The FC calculation of Cal-zld mRNA levels is conducted with the average of control embryos (untreated wild-type and alignment controls) from the same experimental date (embryo batch) as reference. Cal-zld RNAi embryos with a FC < 0.25 (knockdown efficiency greater than 75%) were used for further analysis.

Differential enrichment analysis on the ATAC- and RNA-seq data  will be performed using DESeq2. All experimental groups are used to build the DESeq2 model. The results of the Cal-zld KDs vs alignment control (ac) comparison is reported for both ATAC and RNA-seq DE analysis.


This section will

1) Identify successful Cal-zld KDs

2) Perform DESeq2 on Cal-zld KD RNA- and ATAC-seq data 

3) Perform MEME analysis

4) Present some high-level observations about Cal-zld sensitive peaks (DAPs)

5) Present some high-level observations about genes differentially expressed in (degs) Cal-zld 

Hence forth Cal-zld/Cal-Zld may be shortened to zld/Zld.

```{r}
zld.results.folder<-"../zldKD/"
```


#### Data

##### Create zld coldata from the all.coldata. Filter only samples from the zld experiment.
```{r}
zld.coldata.atac <- all.coldata %>% 
  filter(.,Experiment == "zldKD") 

head(zld.coldata.atac)
```

```{r}
zld.coldata.rna <- all.coldata %>%  
  filter(.,Experiment == "zldKD") 

head(zld.coldata.rna)
```

##### zld ATAC-seq Data

This GRanges object contains all open ATAC-seq reads ( <= 120 bp) for all samples.

Sample names in the GRanges will match information in the columns of the coldata.

The naming convention is coldata$Sample.name.full"."coldata$sample.id.atac.

The Sample.name.full will correspond to only one sample.

```{r, cache = FALSE}
load("../GRanges/zldkd-openreads.GRanges.R")

head(zldkd.openreads)
```


##### zld RNA-seq Data

This GRanges object contains all RNA-seq reads for all samples.

Sample names in the GRanges will match information in the columns of the coldata.

The naming convention is coldata$Sample.name.full"."coldata$sample.id.rna.

The Sample.name.full will correspond to only one sample.

```{r, cache = FALSE}
load("../GRanges/zldkd-rnaseq.GRanges.R")

head(zldkd.rnaseq)
```




### 1. Identify Cal-zld knockdowns

We will identify KDs by calculating the fold change (FC) of zld for each sample.

First we create a count matrix of RNA-seq counts per gene. 

Then we create a CPM matrix that will be used in the FC calculation.

The FC calculation of Cal-zld mRNA levels is conducted with the average of control embryos (untreated wild-type and alignment controls) from the same experimental date (embryo batch) as reference. If a date does not have any wild-type or alignment control embryos fold change will be calculated using the average CPM of all wild-type and alignment control embryos in the data set. 

Cal-zld is evm.TU.scaffold_7.1757 in the annotation

Count overlaps of RNA-seq reads with transcripts.by.gene. 
```{r}
genome(zldkd.rnaseq) <- "ca6" # make sure the genome is specified
zld.counts.rna <- lapply(zldkd.rnaseq, function(x) countOverlaps(transcripts.by.gene,x))
zld.counts.rna <- do.call("cbind",zld.counts.rna) # force the counts data into a table format where rows are genes and columns are samples

head(zld.counts.rna[,1:6])
```

```{r}
zld.colsums <- colSums(zld.counts.rna) # Sum all counts for each sample

zld.cpm <- sweep(x = zld.counts.rna, MARGIN = 2, STATS = zld.colsums, FUN = '/') # For each sample divide each count by the total counts

zld.cpm <- zld.cpm*1e6 # Multiple by 1M to get CPM

table(round(colSums(zld.cpm))) # double check the sum is 1M
```

```{r}
zld.fc.table <- data.frame(Sample.name.full = zld.coldata.rna$Sample.name.full,
                            treatment.group = zld.coldata.rna$treatment.group,
                            Experiment.Date = zld.coldata.rna$Experiment.Date,
                            zld.cpm=zld.cpm["evm.TU.scaffold_7.1757",],
                           actin.cpm=zld.cpm["evm.TU.scaffold_5.1045",])
zld.fc.table%>% mutate(.,zld_to_actin= zld.cpm/actin.cpm)
```

Get the averaged zld CPM for control samples (wt and alignment) by embryo batch.
```{r}

zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date <- zld.fc.table %>% 
  filter(.,treatment.group == "wt" | treatment.group == "alignment control") %>% 
  group_by(.,Experiment.Date) %>% summarize(.,mean(zld.cpm))

```


Add the averaged control CPM to the fc.table, each will have a column. Then perform the FC calculation by dividing each sample's CPM by the control CPM from thesame embryo batch. Add the result to the fc.table, producing the the column called "FC".

Note there are no control samples (wt and alignment) for one embryo batch (240222). In this case, the average of all control samples will be used to calculate the FC of RNAi embryos from that batch.
```{r}

zld.fc.table <- zld.fc.table %>% 
mutate(., zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.231211 = rep(zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date[[1,2]],nrow(zld.fc.table)),
zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.231213 =rep(zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date[[2,2]],nrow(zld.fc.table)),
zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.231218 = rep(zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date[[3,2]],nrow(zld.fc.table))) %>% mutate(., FC =case_when(
  Experiment.Date == "231211" ~ zld.cpm/zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.231211,
  Experiment.Date == "231213" ~ zld.cpm/zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.231213,
  Experiment.Date == "231218" ~ zld.cpm/zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.231218,
  Experiment.Date == "240222" ~ zld.cpm/mean(c(zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date[[1,2]],zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date[[2,2]],zld.cpm.wt.ac.avg.by.date[[3,2]]))))

```


Plot

```{r}

color.code <-c("wt" = "#50ad9f","alignment control" = "#0000A2", "zld"="#800074") 

 zld.fc.table %>% ggplot(., aes(x= treatment.group, y = FC, fill = treatment.group)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 3,shape = 21, color = "black",width=0.2)+

```

4 Cal-zld RNAi embryos have a FC < 0.25




### 2. DE analysis Setup

Add a genotype column to coldata. For the zld treatment group an embryo’s genotype will be either zld, intKD or noKD based on the FC; FC < 0.25 is a KD (zld), 0.25 < FC < 0.5 is an intermediate KD (intKD) and FC > 0.5 is no KD (noKD). For the control treatment groups, genotype is equal to the treatment group, but written in short hand.

Starting with the zld.coldata.rna.
```{r}
zld.coldata.rna <- cbind(zld.coldata.rna, FC = zld.fc.table$FC)

zld.coldata.rna <- zld.coldata.rna %>%
  mutate(genotype = case_when(
  treatment.group == "wt" ~ "wt",
  treatment.group == "alignment control" ~ "ac",
  #(treatment.group == "zld" & FC<1.5&FC > 0.5) ~ "noKD",
  #(treatment.group == "zld" & FC>1.5) ~ "outlier",
  (treatment.group == "zld" & FC > 0.5) ~ "noKD",
  (treatment.group == "zld" & 0.25 < FC & FC < 0.5) ~ "intKD",
   (treatment.group == "zld" & FC < 0.25) ~ "zld")) %>% 
  relocate(.,genotype,.after = treatment.group)

#convert all columns to factors
for (i in 1:ncol(zld.coldata.rna)){
    zld.coldata.rna[, i] = as.factor(zld.coldata.rna[, i])
}

# set ref levels
zld.coldata.rna$treatment.group <- relevel(zld.coldata.rna$treatment.group,ref = "alignment control")

zld.coldata.rna$genotype <- relevel(zld.coldata.rna$genotype,ref = "ac")

zld.coldata.rna$Experiment.Date <- relevel(zld.coldata.rna$Experiment.Date,ref = "231213")

head(zld.coldata.rna)

```

Add the column names of the counts matrix to the rownames of the coldata. Double check that all match.
```{r}
#cbind(as.character(zld.coldata.rna$Sample.name.full),colnames(zld.counts.rna))

rownames(zld.coldata.rna) <- colnames(zld.counts.rna)

all(colnames(zld.counts.rna) == rownames(zld.coldata.rna))
```

Now repeat for the coldata.atac
```{r}
zld.coldata.atac <- cbind(zld.coldata.atac, FC = zld.fc.table$FC)

zld.coldata.atac <- zld.coldata.atac %>%
  mutate(genotype = case_when(
  treatment.group == "wt" ~ "wt",
  treatment.group == "alignment control" ~ "ac",
  #(treatment.group == "zld" & FC<1.5&FC > 0.5) ~ "noKD",
  #(treatment.group == "zld" & FC>1.5) ~ "outlier",
  (treatment.group == "zld" & FC > 0.5) ~ "noKD",
  (treatment.group == "zld" & 0.25 < FC & FC < 0.5) ~ "intKD",
   (treatment.group == "zld" & FC < 0.25) ~ "zld")) %>% 
  relocate(.,genotype,.after = treatment.group)

#convert all columns to factors
for (i in 1:ncol(zld.coldata.atac)){
    zld.coldata.atac[, i] = as.factor(zld.coldata.atac[, i])
}


# set ref levels
zld.coldata.atac$treatment.group <- relevel(zld.coldata.atac$treatment.group,ref = "alignment control")

zld.coldata.atac$genotype <- relevel(zld.coldata.atac$genotype,ref = "ac")

zld.coldata.atac$Experiment.Date <- relevel(zld.coldata.atac$Experiment.Date,ref = "231213")


head(zld.coldata.atac)
```

Create the counts matrix for zldKD ATAC-seq data
```{r}
zld.counts.atac <- lapply(zldkd.openreads, function(x) countOverlaps(peaks.32157, x)) # count open reads that overlap with a peak
zld.counts.atac <- do.call("cbind", zld.counts.atac) # coerce to a matrix

head(zld.counts.atac[,1:6])
```

Add the column names of the counts matrix to the rownames of the coldata. Double check that all match.
```{r}
#cbind(as.character(zld.coldata.atac$Sample.name.full),colnames(zld.counts.atac))

rownames(zld.coldata.atac) <- colnames(zld.counts.atac)

all(colnames(zld.counts.atac) == rownames(zld.coldata.atac))
```

##### Filter counts

Before proceeding with the DESeq2 analysis, the RNA-seq counts need to be filtered to remove noisy and no count genes. This will be done by plotting the distribution of counts, which will show the true distribution and the noise. A cutoff based on the count distribution will be applied to remove any counts below those values.

```{r}
data.frame(means = log2(rowMeans(zld.counts.rna)+1)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(means)) +
  geom_density() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5) +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = 'Distribution of rna counts zld KD experiment')
```

Remove any gene counts below 2^5
```{r}
zld.counts.rna <- zld.counts.rna[which(rowMeans(zld.counts.rna) > 2^5),]
```

Again check that the colnames in the counts matrix match the rownames in coldata.
```{r}
all(colnames(zld.counts.rna) == rownames(zld.coldata.rna))
```



##### Filter ATAC counts

Before running DESeq2 we need to get rid of any peaks that have low or noisy counts.
```{r}
data.frame(sums = log2(rowSums(zld.counts.atac)+1)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(sums)) +
  geom_density() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 6.5) +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = 'Distribution of atac counts zldKD experiment')
```

The number of peaks from the distribution above with counts less than 2^6.5.
```{r}
length(which(rowSums(zld.counts.atac) < 2^6.5))
```

The number of peaks with any count value of 0 or 1.
```{r}
table(apply(zld.counts.atac, 1, function(x) sum(x <= 1)))
```

We will filter peaks that have any count value of 0 or 1.
```{r}
zld.counts.atac <- zld.counts.atac[apply(zld.counts.atac, 1, function(x) !any(x <= 1)),]
```

This removes low count peaks form the distribution above.
```{r}
length(which(rowSums(zld.counts.atac) < 2^6.5))
```

Again check that the colnames in the counts matrix match the rownames in coldata.
```{r}
all(colnames(zld.counts.atac) == rownames(zld.coldata.atac))
```


### 3.DESeq2 RNA-seq data

The design component for RNA-seq and ATAC-seq the DESeq2 analysis with be the same. The design component will include embryo batch (Experiment.Date) and genotype. We are interested in the changes in expression/accessibility due to genotype, this variable will be added last in the design.
```{r}
zld.rna.dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = zld.counts.rna, colData = zld.coldata.rna, design = ~ Experiment.Date + genotype)
zld.rna.dds <- DESeq(zld.rna.dds, parallel = FALSE)
```

```{r}
zld.rna.norm_counts <- counts(zld.rna.dds , normalized=TRUE)


noKD_samples <- rownames(colData(zld.rna.dds))[zld.rna.dds$genotype == "noKD"]
AC_samples <- rownames(colData(zld.rna.dds))[zld.rna.dds$genotype == "ac"]

# 3. Get the sample sizes (n)
n_noKD_samples <- length(noKD_samples)
n_AC_samples  <- length(AC_samples )

# 4. Calculate the Standard Error on the normalized counts
# rowSds calculates the sample standard deviation (s), then we divide by sqrt(n)
se_norm_noKD_samples <- sum(rowSds(zld.rna.norm_counts[, noKD_samples]) / sqrt(n_noKD_samples))
se_norm_n_AC_samples <- sum(rowSds(zld.rna.norm_counts[, AC_samples]) / sqrt(n_AC_samples ))
```



Check that the names of results are as expected.
```{r}
resultsNames(zld.rna.dds)
```

Dispersion estimates. Take a look at dispersion to makes sure that the data fitting looks reasonable.
```{r}
plotDispEsts(zld.rna.dds)
```

Results 

##### zld vs zldnoKD control DE genes
```{r}

res.zldnoKD.ac.rna<-as.data.frame(results(zld.rna.dds, contrast = c("genotype", "noKD", "ac"), independentFiltering = FALSE))
```

Add a column, “Sig”, indicating if a gene is significantly differential expressed.

Significant DEGs will be genes with a LFC >= 1 or LFC <=-1 and a padj <= 0.05

### 4.DESeq2 ATAC-seq data

```{r}
zld.atac.dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = zld.counts.atac, colData = zld.coldata.atac, design = ~ Experiment.Date + genotype)
zld.atac.dds <- DESeq(zld.atac.dds, parallel = FALSE)
```

Check that the names of results are as expected.
```{r}
resultsNames(zld.atac.dds)
```

Dispersion estimates. Take a look at dispersion to makes sure that the data fitting looks reasonable.
```{r}
plotDispEsts(zld.atac.dds)

```
##### zldKD vs alignment control DA peaks
```{r}
res.zld.ac.atac <- as.data.frame(results(zld.atac.dds, contrast = c("genotype", "zld", "ac"), independentFiltering = FALSE))
```

Add a column, "Sig", indicating if a peak has undergone a significantly change in accessibility.

Significant DAPs will be peaks with a LFC >= 1 or LFC <=-1 and a padj <= 0.05

```{r}
res.zld.ac.atac <- res.zld.ac.atac %>% mutate(.,Sig = if_else((padj <= 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) >=1),TRUE,FALSE))
```

Add a column, "Change", indicating if the change in accessibility was up or down.
```{r}
res.zld.ac.atac <- res.zld.ac.atac %>% 
  mutate(Change = case_when(is.na(log2FoldChange) == TRUE | Sig == FALSE ~ "NA",
  log2FoldChange < 0 ~ "DOWN",
  log2FoldChange > 0 ~ "UP"))
```

Add a column, "peak.name", with the peak name.
```{r}
res.zld.ac.atac <- res.zld.ac.atac %>% mutate(.,peak.name=rownames(.))
res.zld.ac.atac$gene_locus<-peak_annotation[match(res.zld.ac.atac$peak.name, row.names(peak_annotation)),]$geneId
```

MA plot
```{r}
res.zld.ac.atac %>% 
  mutate(sig = padj <= 0.05) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log10(baseMean), y = log2FoldChange, color = sig)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-5,5)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" =  "black")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0,1,-1), linetype = 'dotted', color = 'blue') +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = "MA Plot res.zld.ac.atac",
       x = "log10(mean counts)",
       y = "log2(FC)")
```


Lets plot the result and highlight significant DAPs. For this plot sig DAPs will be highlighted, and the number of DAPs that go up or down will be quantified. The size of each data point will correspond to the intensity of the peak.



```{r }
#pdf(file = "../vol_zldvsAC.pdf", width = 5,height = 5)

zld.ac.vol.atac <- res.zld.ac.atac %>% 
  mutate(mean.intensity = baseMean/max(baseMean)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), color = Change, size = mean.intensity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-10, 10), ylim = c(0, 50)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log2(c(0.5, 2)), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN" = 'red', "UP" = "blue", "NA" = "grey")) +
 
  theme_clean(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "none")+
  
  # Optional: Fine-tune specific elements if base_size isn't enough
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(title = 'zldKD vs AC DA peaks at LNC14')


zld.ac.vol.atac  + 

  annotate(geom = "text", x = -4, y = 28, 
           label = length(which(res.zld.ac.atac$padj <= 0.05 & res.zld.ac.atac$log2FoldChange <= -1)), 
           size = 5) + 
  
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 4, y = 28, 
           label = length(which(res.zld.ac.atac$padj <= 0.05 & res.zld.ac.atac$log2FoldChange >= 1)), 
           size = 5) +
  
  annotate(geom = 'text', x = 0, y = 27, 
           label = length(which(res.zld.ac.atac$padj <= 0.05 & abs(res.zld.ac.atac$log2FoldChange) < 1)), 
           size = 5)
#dev.off()
```

Lets plot the result and highlight significant DAPs. For this plot sig DAPs will be highlighted, and the number of DAPs that go up or down will be quantified. The size of each data point will correspond to the intensity of the peak.
```{r}

#pdf(file = "../vol_wt_vs_ac.pdf", width = 5,height = 5)

wt.ac.vol.atac <- res.wt.ac.atac %>% 
  mutate(mean.intensity = baseMean/max(baseMean, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), color = Change, size = mean.intensity)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-10, 10), ylim = c(0, 50)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log2(c(0.5, 2)), linetype = 'dashed', col = 'orange') +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN" = 'red', "UP" = "blue", "NS" = "grey")) +
  theme_clean(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "none")+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12)
  ) +
  labs(title = 'WT vs AC DA peaks')

wt.ac.vol.atac + 
  annotate(geom = "text", x = -4, y = 28, 
           label = sum(res.wt.ac.atac$padj <= 0.05 & res.wt.ac.atac$log2FoldChange <= -1), 
           size = 5) + 
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 4, y = 28, 
           label = sum(res.wt.ac.atac$padj <= 0.05 & res.wt.ac.atac$log2FoldChange >= 1), 
           size = 5) +
  annotate(geom = 'text', x = 0, y = 27, 
           label = sum(res.wt.ac.atac$padj <= 0.05 & abs(res.wt.ac.atac$log2FoldChange) < 1), 
           size = 5)

#dev.off()

```

### 5. MEME Cal-zld KD

We will use MEME to identify motifs enriched in Cal-zld sensitive peaks.

MEME will be performed on all Cal-zld sensitive peaks, Cal-zld sensitive peaks that lose accessibility and Cal-zld sensitive peaks that gain accessibility. 

We will extract sequences for each peak group and for a set of background sequences as done in previous sections.
```{r}
zld.ac.daps.up <- res.zld.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP") %>% rownames()

zld.ac.daps.down <- res.zld.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()

zld.ac.daps.all <- res.zld.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP" | Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()

zld.ac.daps.BG<-res.zld.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == FALSE)%>%rownames()

```

```{r}
zld.noKD.daps.up <- res.zld.noKD.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP") %>% rownames()

zld.noKD.daps.down <- res.zld.noKD.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()

zld.noKD.daps.all <- res.zld.noKD.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP" | Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()

zld.noKD.daps.BG<-res.zld.noKD.atac%>%filter(.,Sig == FALSE) %>% rownames()

```
```{r}
wt.ac.daps.up <- res.wt.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP") %>% rownames()

wt.ac.daps.down <- res.wt.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()

wt.ac.daps.all <- res.wt.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP" | Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()

wt.ac.daps.BG<-res.wt.ac.atac %>%filter(.,Sig == FALSE) %>% rownames()

```


```{r}
zldnoKD.ac.daps.up <- res.zldnoKD.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP") %>% rownames()

zldnoKD.ac.daps.down <- res.zldnoKD.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()

zldnoKD.ac.daps.all <- res.zldnoKD.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP" | Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN") %>% rownames()

zldnoKD.ac.daps.BG<-res.zldnoKD.ac.atac %>% filter(.,Sig == FALSE ) %>% rownames()

```

peaks that are not sensitive to any treatment as background for MEME analysis
```{r}

zld.daps.all.BG<-common_names <- Reduce(intersect, list(zld.ac.daps.BG,wt.ac.daps.BG,zld.noKD.daps.BG, zldnoKD.ac.daps.BG))
```


Get sequences for each peak group using the get.my.seqs function.
```{r eval=FALSE}
sequence.output.directory <-"../MEME"
# dir for output
set.seed(124) # set seed for sampling

bgset <- sample(peaks.32157[zld.daps.all.BG], size = 1000)
start(bgset) <- bgset$max
end(bgset) <- bgset$max
bgset <- resize(bgset, width = 100, fix = "center")
bgseqs <- getSeq(Calbipunctata, bgset)

export(bgseqs, con = paste0(sequence.output.directory, "/zld-BGall-1K.txt"), format = "fasta")

get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% zld.ac.daps.down], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "zld.ac-daps-down")
get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% zld.ac.daps.up], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "zld.ac-daps-up")
get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% zld.ac.daps.all], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "zld.ac-daps-all")


get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% zldnoKD.ac.daps.down], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "zldnoKD.ac-daps-down")
get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% zldnoKD.ac.daps.up], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "zldnoKD.ac-daps-up")
get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% zldnoKD.ac.daps.all], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "zldnoKD.ac-daps-all")


get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157)%in% zld.noKD.daps.down], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "zld.noKD-daps-down")
get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% zld.noKD.daps.up], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "zld.noKD-daps-up")
get.my.seqs(p = peaks.32157[names(peaks.32157) %in% zld.noKD.daps.all], dir = sequence.output.directory, name = "zld.noKD-daps-all")

get.my.seqs(p= peaks.32157[zld.daps.all.BG], dir= sequence.output.directory, name = "zld-daps-allBG")
```


#### Find zld PWM 2 


Load in the PWM from MEME. This is already a freq matrix.
```{r, cache = FALSE}

zldPWM2 <- as.matrix(read.table("../PWMs/zld-meme-nc11-motif6-TACCTG_freqs.txt", header = FALSE, sep =" "))

colnames(zldPWM2) <- c("A","C","G","T")
```

```{r}
tzldPWM2 <- t(zldPWM2)
seqLogo(tzldPWM2)
# There are no low information positions to trim.

```

Save PWM.
```{r eval=FALSE}
pdf(file = "../Plots/zld-meme-rc.pdf", width = 6,height = 5)

seqLogo(tzldPWM2)

dev.off()

```

(We will save time and skip this part, the updated motif table can be found in ./WT_timecourse/motif-table.txt) 

zld PWM 2 in peaks. 
```{r eval=FALSE}
zld.peak.2 <- lapply(seq.peaks, function(x){
  matchPWM(tzldPWM2, subject = x, min.score = "80%",with.score = TRUE)
})

zld.peak.rc.2 <- lapply(seq.peaks, function(x){
  matchPWM(tzldPWM2RevCom, subject = x, min.score = "80%",with.score = TRUE)
})
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
# peaks with at least one match will have a length greater than 0
n.zld.peak.2 <- zld.peak.2[lengths(zld.peak.2) > 0]  
n.zld.peak.rc.2 <- zld.peak.rc.2[lengths(zld.peak.rc.2) > 0] 
```


```{r eval=FALSE}
paste0("percent of peaks with a zld MEME motif ",
       round(length(unique(c(names(n.zld.peak.2),names(n.zld.peak.rc.2))))/(length(peaks.32157))*100,1),"%")

```

Percent of peaks with either Zld motif
```{r eval=FALSE}
paste0("percent of peaks with a zld motif ",
       round(length(unique(c(names(n.zld.peak),names(n.zld.peak.rc),names(n.zld.peak.2),names(n.zld.peak.rc.2))))/(length(peaks.32157))*100,1),"%")
```

Update the motif table
```{r eval=FALSE}
zld.peaks.2.l <- names(peaks.32157) %in% names(n.zld.peak.2)
zld.peaks.rc.2.l <- names(peaks.32157) %in% names(n.zld.peak.rc.2)
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
motif.table<-read_delim("../WT_timecourse/motif-table.txt")
motif.table <- data.frame(motif.table,
          zld.sites.2 = zld.peaks.2.l,
           zld.sites.rc.2 = zld.peaks.rc.2.l)


#head(motif.table)
```

All of the peaks with the first zld PWM also have the second MEME derived zld PWM
```{r eval=FALSE}
all(motif.table[motif.table$zld.sites == TRUE | motif.table$zld.sites.rc,]$peak.name %in% motif.table[motif.table$zld.sites.2 == TRUE | motif.table$zld.sites.rc.2,]$peak.name)
```


SAVE updated motif table

```{r eval=FALSE}
write.table(motif.table,file = "../WT_timecourse/motif-table.txt", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE)
```

###### peak up&down binomial test
```{r}
# Define the counts for the first group (k) and the total counts (n) for each comparison
k_values <- c(2399, 278, 1632, 484)
n_values <- c(2399 + 1703, 278 + 450, 1632 + 513, 484 + 450)
comparison_names <- c("Comp 1", "Comp 2", "Comp 3", "Comp 4")

# Create a data frame for results
results <- data.frame(
  Comparison = comparison_names,
  Count_k = k_values,
  Count_Total = n_values,
  P_value = NA,
  Proportion = k_values / n_values
)

# Run the Binomial Test for each comparison
for (i in 1:length(k_values)) {
  test_result <- binom.test(
    x = k_values[i], 
    n = n_values[i], 
    p = 0.5, 
  )
  results$P_value[i] <- test_result$p.value
}

# Print the results
print(results)
```

```{r}
  imap(function(df, name) {
    df %>%

  }) %>%

Genomic_features_summary_down<- df_list_down %>%

  }) %>%

Genomic_features_summary_up<- df_list_up %>%
```

##### Cal-zld sensitive peaks and dynamic peaks

From the above we observe that peaks that gain or lose accessibility upon Cal-zld KD are in different dynamic classes. Notably peaks that gain accessibility upon Cal-zld depletion are in groups of peaks who lose accessibility as nuclear cycles progress. Conversely peaks that lose accessibility upon Cal-zld KD are peaks that gain accessibility as nuclear cycles progress. See (Dynamic groups plot , patterns$plot)

We will test if membership in any dynamic group selects for Cal-zld sensitivity (gain or loss of accessibility) more frequently than we would expect from random chance.  This will be done by using R functions to perform uses the odds ratio and fishers test on basic contingency tables denoting presence/absence in a dynamic group and Cal-zld sensitivity/insensitivity.

First we will reorganize the data

We will use the table with the dynamic/non dynamic classification of peaks.
```{r}
patterns.group.table<-read.delim("../WT_timecourse/patterns-group-table.txt")
head(patterns.group.table)
```

Now we will create a new table "zld.daps.dynamics". This table contains the name of the peak "peak.name", a column "Change.in.zld" denoting if a the change in accessibility was UP or DOWN and a column "class" denoting the peak's dynamic group or non dynamic classification.

Note: not all of the mater peaks were included in the Cal-zld DE analysis, recall that peaks with  low count values are removed before DESeq2 analysis. 

```{r}
zld.daps.dynamics <- res.zld.ac.atac %>% 
  merge(x=.,y=patterns.group.table, by = "peak.name",all.x = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(class = case_when(
  group.1 == TRUE ~ "group.1",
  group.2 == TRUE ~ "group.2",
  group.3 == TRUE ~ "group.3",
  group.4 == TRUE ~ "group.4",
  group.5 == TRUE ~ "group.5",
  group.6 == TRUE ~ "group.6",
  group.7 == TRUE ~ "group.7",
  group.8 == TRUE ~ "group.8",
  group.9 == TRUE ~ "group.9",
  group.10 == TRUE ~ "group.10",
  group.11 == TRUE ~ "group.11",
  group.12 == TRUE ~ "group.12",
  group.13 == TRUE ~ "group.13",
  group.14 == TRUE ~ "group.14",
  group.15 == TRUE ~ "group.15",
  group.16 == TRUE ~ "group.16",
  group.17 == TRUE ~ "group.17",
  group.18 == TRUE ~ "group.18",
  group.19 == TRUE ~ "group.19",
  group.20 == TRUE ~ "group.20",
  group.21 == TRUE ~ "group.21",
  dynamic.peak == TRUE & dynamic.in.class == FALSE ~ "dynamic not in group",
  dynamic.peak == FALSE & dynamic.in.class == FALSE ~ "not dynamic not in group")) %>%
   mutate(.,Change.in.zld = case_when(Sig == TRUE & Change == "UP" ~ "UP", 
                                     Sig == TRUE & Change == "DOWN" ~ "DOWN", 
                                     is.na(Sig) & Change == "DOWN" ~ "NA", 
                                     is.na(Sig) & Change == "UP" ~ "NA")) %>% 
  mutate(Change.in.zld = if_else(is.na(Change.in.zld),"Not affected",Change.in.zld)) %>% 
  mutate(Change.in.zld = if_else(Change.in.zld == "NA","Not affected",Change.in.zld)) %>% select(c(peak.name,Change.in.zld,class))

head(zld.daps.dynamics)

```


We will use the "zld.daps.dynamics" to perform the odds ratio and fisher test. 

Each group Cal-zld sensitive DOWN, Cal-zld sensitive UP and Not affect will be tested separately.

First Cal-zld sensitive DOWN. 

Below constructs the contingency table, performs the odds ratio and fisher test for each dynamic/non-dynamic group. The output is a long list, which in following chunks will be turned into a dataframe.
```{r}
groupnames = unique(zld.daps.dynamics$class)

fisher.down = sapply(groupnames, function(x) {
  contingency = matrix(c(
    "down_inclass" = sum(zld.daps.dynamics$Change.in.zld == "DOWN" & zld.daps.dynamics$class == x),
    "down_!inclass" = sum(zld.daps.dynamics$Change.in.zld == "DOWN" & !zld.daps.dynamics$class == x),
    "!down_inclass" = sum(!zld.daps.dynamics$Change.in.zld == "DOWN" & zld.daps.dynamics$class == x),
    "!down_!inclass" = sum(!zld.daps.dynamics$Change.in.zld == "DOWN" & !zld.daps.dynamics$class == x)
  ), 
  nrow = 2, 
  byrow = TRUE
  )
  
  f = fisher.test(contingency)
  return(list(pval = f$p.value, log2odds = log2(f$estimate), table = contingency))
}, simplify = FALSE)

head(fisher.down)
```


Lets make this a df so that it is easier to work with.
```{r}
fisher.down.df <- lapply(fisher.down, function(x){unlist(x[1:3])})
fisher.down.df <- do.call("rbind",fisher.down.df)

fisher.down.df <- as.data.frame(fisher.down.df)

head(fisher.down.df)

```

Now will add the class column, and fix the column names.
```{r}
fisher.down.df <- fisher.down.df %>% 
  mutate(class = rownames(.)) %>% 
  relocate(class,.before = pval) %>% 
  rename("pval.fish.down" = pval,
         "log2odds.odds.ratio.fish.down" = `log2odds.odds ratio`,
         "YY.fish.down" = table1,
         "NY.fish.down" = table2,
         "YN.fish.down" = table3,
         "NN.fish.down" = table4)


head(fisher.down.df)
```



These groups are likely to be dynamic peak groups whose accessibility is Cal-zld dependent. We will select for groups that have a log2(odd ratio) greater than 1.5.
```{r}
fisher.down.df %>% filter(log2odds.odds.ratio.fish.down > 1.5)
```

Cal-zld sensitive UP.
```{r}
fisher.up = sapply(groupnames, function(x) {
  contingency = matrix(c(
    "up_inclass" = sum(zld.daps.dynamics$Change.in.zld == "UP" & zld.daps.dynamics$class == x),
    "up_!inclass" = sum(zld.daps.dynamics$Change.in.zld == "UP" & !zld.daps.dynamics$class == x),
    "!up_inclass" = sum(!zld.daps.dynamics$Change.in.zld == "UP" & zld.daps.dynamics$class == x),
    "!up_!inclass" = sum(!zld.daps.dynamics$Change.in.zld == "UP" & !zld.daps.dynamics$class == x)
  ), 
  nrow = 2, 
  byrow = TRUE
  )
  
  f = fisher.test(contingency)
  return(list(pval = f$p.value, log2odds = log2(f$estimate), table = contingency))
}, simplify = FALSE)
```

```{r}
level.order = c("not dynamic not in group","group.8","group.15","group.14","group.12","group.6","group.10","group.9","group.4","group.11","group.16","group.21","group.19","group.20","group.17","group.2","group.18","group.7","group.13","group.3","group.5","group.1")

```



```{r eval=FALSE}

pdf(file = "../Plots/zld-daps-dynamic-bar-plot-LABEL2.pdf", width = 10,height = 10)

zld.ac.daps.dynamic.peaks %>% 
  # 1. First, strictly keep only UP and DOWN data.
  # This removes "Not affected" rows so they don't generate unwanted zeros.
  filter(Change %in% c("UP", "DOWN")) %>% 
  
  ungroup() %>% 
  
  # 2. Ensure every group has exactly one UP and one DOWN row
  complete(class = level.order, Change = c("UP", "DOWN"), 
           fill = list(n = 0, percent.by.change = 0)) %>% 
  
  # 3. Setup factor levels and calculate plotting values
  mutate(
    class = factor(class, levels = level.order),
    # Make DOWN values negative for the butterfly plot
    n_plot = if_else(Change == "DOWN", -1 * n, n),
    # Pre-calculate label text
    label_text = paste0(n, " (", percent.by.change, "%)"),
    # Pre-calculate alignment: DOWN goes left (1.1), UP goes right (-0.1)
    label_hjust = if_else(Change == "DOWN", 1.1, -0.1)
  ) %>% 
  
  # 4. Plot
  ggplot(aes(x = class, y = n_plot, fill = Change)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.8, colour = "black") +
  
  # Standard geom_text (No hiding filter, as requested)
  geom_text(aes(label = label_text, hjust = label_hjust), size = 3) +
  
  scale_x_discrete(limits = level.order) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = abs, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.3, 0.3))) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("DOWN" = 'darkred', "UP" = "darkblue")) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(axis.line.y = element_line(colour = "black"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.grid = element_blank()) + 
  labs(y = "Number of Peaks", x = "Peak Class")

dev.off()
```

### 7. High-level observations about genes differentially expressed in (degs) Cal-zld 

#### Gene expression profile by stages

Below is the number of DEGs upon Cal-zld KD.
```{r}
res.zldnoKD.ac.rna %>%
  count(Sig) %>% 
  mutate(percent = round((n / sum(n)) * 100,1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) 
```

Below is the % of DEGs whose expression decreases or increases.
```{r}
res.zldnoKD.ac.rna %>% 
  filter(.,Sig != "NA") %>%
  mutate(Change = case_when(
  Change == "UP" ~ "UP",
  Change == "DOWN" ~ "DOWN",
  Change == "NA" ~ "Not affected")) %>% 
  count(Change) %>% 
  mutate(percent = round((n / sum(n)) * 100,1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n)) 
```

Now we want to determine the maternal vs zygotic identify of Cal-zld DEGs.

First we need to identify genes whose expression is  maternal, zygotic, maternal-zygotic or neither.

To do so we will create a count threshold for each gene in NC2/3 (~45 min old, before zygotic transcription, enriched in maternally deposited mRNAs) and syncytial embryos (NC11-Late NC14)


We will load WT RNA-seq timecourse data.

Sample order: 1-4 NC2/3/maternal, 5-8 NC11, 9-12 NC12, 13-16 NC13, 17-20 NC14, 21-24 LNC14
```{r, cache = FALSE}
load("../GRanges/wt-tc-rnaseq.GRanges.R")

head(wt.tc.rnaseq)
```

Count overlaps of RNA-seq reads with transcripts.by.gene. 
```{r}
genome(wt.tc.rnaseq) <- "ca6" # make sure the genome is specified
wt.counts.rna <- lapply(wt.tc.rnaseq, function(x) countOverlaps(transcripts.by.gene,x))
wt.counts.rna <- do.call("cbind",wt.counts.rna) # force the counts data into a table format where rows are genes and columns are samples

head(wt.counts.rna[,1:6])
```

Distribution of gene counts of maternal samples. 

The low point is ~2^5. This distribution picks up after.
```{r}
data.frame(means = log2(rowMeans(wt.counts.rna[,1:4])+1)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(means)) +
  geom_density() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5) +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = 'Distribution of counts for maternal samples')
```

Distribution of gene counts of syncytial (zygotic) samples. 

The low point is likewise around 2^5. 
```{r}
data.frame(means = log2(rowMeans(wt.counts.rna[,5:24])+1)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(means)) +
  geom_density() + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5) +
  theme_clean() +
  labs(title = 'Distribution of counts for zygotic samples')
```


Now we will identify genes expressed in maternal or zyotic stages based on the distributions above. 

We will use the thresholds of 2^5. 

*maternal*
First create an index of the row positions. Then extract the row name corresponding to the gene name (rowname = gene name).
```{r}
mat.index <- which(rowMeans(wt.counts.rna[,1:4]) > 2^5)
#mat.index
mat.genes <- rownames(wt.counts.rna[mat.index,])
```


*zygotic*
Repeat the process for zygotic genes.
```{r}
zyg.index <-  which(rowMeans(wt.counts.rna[,5:24]) > 2^5)

zyg.genes <- rownames(wt.counts.rna[zyg.index,])
```



Create a df summarizing the maternal-zygotic expression of a gene. Column, "gene.locus" will contain the gene name. Columns, "maternal" and "zygotic", will be T/F indicating if the gene was expressed or not at the respective developmental stage. We will create a final column "MZ" indicating if the gene is strictly maternal, strictly zygotic, both maternal zygotic or neither. 

```{r}
mz.df <- data.frame(gene.locus = rownames(wt.counts.rna))
```

```{r}
mz.df <- mz.df %>% 
  mutate(maternal = gene.locus %in% mat.genes) %>% 
  mutate(zygotic = gene.locus %in% zyg.genes) %>% 
  mutate(MZ=case_when(
  maternal == TRUE & zygotic == TRUE ~  "maternal zygotic",
  maternal == FALSE & zygotic == FALSE ~  "neither",
  maternal == TRUE & zygotic == FALSE ~  "maternal",
  maternal == FALSE & zygotic == TRUE ~  "zygotic"))

mz.df %>% head()
```

Below is the distribution of the MZ column. 
```{r}
mz.df %>% count(.,MZ)
```
```{r eval=FALSE}
write.csv(mz.df, "../WT_timecourse/mz.df.csv")
```

```{r}
)
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
     main = FALSE,

     edges = TRUE # Keep the circle edges visible
```

```{r}
))
```

# Section 4 Gene loci visualization 

### plotting functions
function for smoothing big wig/wiggle files for plotting
```{r}
wigsmooth = function(x){
    a = score(x)
    b = zoo::rollmean(zoo::as.zoo(a), 10)
    c = rep(0, length(a))
    c[zoo::index(b)] = b
    score(x) = c
    return(x)
}
```

Gvizzer funciton to plot ATAC and RNA-seq data
```{r}
gvizzer = function(ROI, # region of interest
                   view.width = NULL, # resize, or NULL chooses the size of the ROI
                   counts = bw, # GRangesList with counts
                   nplots = 5, # how many of the GRangesList elements to plot?
                   title = "", # text appended to the plotted genome coordinates title
                   shifter = 0, # how much to nudge the ROI to the right or left
                   txstack = "dense", # dense or full display of the gene region track
                   scalebar = 1000, # scale bar length in bp
                   trackcols = c(
                       "darkorchid4", 
                       "darkorchid4", 
                       "cornflowerblue", 
                       "cornflowerblue",
                       "grey"
                   ), # a vector of colors for each plotted element in 'counts'
                   plotType = c(rep("histogram", 4), 'histogram'), # plot type
                   ymin = c(0, 0, 0, 0, -1.25), # y-axis minimum value per plot
                   ymax = c(40, 40, 40, 40, 1.25) # y-axis maximum value per plot
) {
    
    # note, in this version, the nplots value should be equal to the number of
    # specified colors, and the number of elements in the ymin and ymax vectors.
    require(Gviz)
    require(GenomicRanges)
    require(BSgenome.Calbipunctata.Cantata.uni4000)
    
    oregion = GRanges(ROI)
    
    if(is.null(view.width)){view.width = width(oregion)}
    
    chr = as.character(seqnames(oregion))
    region = resize(oregion, width = view.width, fix = "center")
    start(region) = start(region) + shifter
    end(region) = end(region) + shifter
    
    from = as.numeric(start(region))
    to = as.numeric(end(region))
    
    title = paste0(title, ": ", region)
    options(ucscChromosomeNames=FALSE) # required, otherwise Gviz will expect usc formatted chr names ie chr1 etc
    grtrack = GeneRegionTrack(
        calbi.txdb, 
        genome = "ca6", 
        from = from, 
        to = to, 
        chromosome = chr, 
        stacking = txstack
        )
    
    gtr = GenomeAxisTrack(scale = scalebar)
    
    dts = list()
    
    for(i in 1 : nplots)
    {
        dts[[i]] = DataTrack(
            counts[[i]],
            name = names(counts)[i],
            type = plotType[i],
            ylim=c(ymin[i], ymax[i]),
            col.histogram = rgb(t(col2rgb(trackcols[i])/255), alpha = 0), # make the border transparent.
            fill.histogram = trackcols[i],
            col.mountain = trackcols[i],
            fill.mountain = rep(trackcols[i], 2)
            )
    }
    # note that specifying colors for different kinds of plot types does not throw an error
    # this means it is easy to write a general for-loop to generate the data tracks
    # and still be able to choose different plot types in the options for the function.
    
    plotTracks(
        trackList = c(list(gtr), dts[c(1:nplots)], list(grtrack)), 
        from = from, 
        to = to, 
        chromosome = chr, 
        main = title, 
        cex.main = 1
    )
}
```

```{r}
gvizzer(ROI= zld.locus, 
        counts = tc.rna.bw, 
        view.width = width(zld.locus), 
        nplots = 6,
        shifter = 0,
        title = 'zld locus',
        txstack = "dense",
        scalebar = 1000 ,
        trackcols = c(rep("#122740",6)),
        plotType = rep("polygon", 6),
        ymin = c(rep(0,6)),
        ymax = c(rep(120,6)))


#dev.off()
```
